<image-desc>The seal of the Theosophical Society. At the very top is the Sanskrit character for "Om" <note>A sacred sound and a spiritual symbol in Indian religions, signifying the essence of the ultimate reality</note>. Below it is a circular emblem featuring an Ouroboros <note>A serpent eating its own tail, representing eternity and the cycle of life and death</note>. Inside the serpent's circle are two interlaced triangles forming a hexagram; at its center is an Ankh <note>An ancient Egyptian symbol of life</note>, and at the top point of the hexagram is a swastika <note>An ancient symbol of good fortune and cosmic order, used here in its original spiritual context</note> enclosed in a small circle. Inscribed around the inner edge of the serpent is the motto "THERE IS NO RELIGION HIGHER THAN TRUTH."</image-desc>

### SECTION 11—THE DEVIL IS GOD INVERTED <note>original: "DEMON EST DEUS INVERSUS"</note> . . . 129

## PART 3. SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL <note>original: "ADDENDA"</note>

### SECTION 1—REASONS FOR THESE SUPPLEMENTS . . . . 199
No conflict exists between hidden <note>original: "Occult"</note> science and modern empirical science <note>original: "Exact Science"</note> whenever the conclusions of the latter are based on undeniable facts — Forces are intelligent and are divine beings <note>original: "Devas and Genii"</note> — The Sun is composed of both matter and spirit — The Sun gives life to the physical world, while the hidden Spirit-Sun gives life and light to the spiritual and mental realms.

### SECTION 2—MODERN PHYSICISTS ARE FUMBLING IN THE DARK <note>original: "PLAYING BLIND-MAN'S-BUFF"</note> . . . 205
Science must learn the true reality of matter, atoms, the ether, and force — Is light a physical substance or not? — Contradictory theories — Perspectives on the nature of the ether — Practitioners of the hidden sciences <note>original: "Occultists"</note> say that the creator of nature is nature itself.

### SECTION 3—IS GRAVITATION A LAW? . . . 213
Scientific views on gravity — Pythagoras and Plato on the rulers of the planets — Fohat <note>In Theosophy, the active force that connects spirit and matter, often described as "cosmic electricity."</note>, the energizing and guiding intelligence within the universal electrical life-fluid — Forces in nature are intelligent, individual entities — Newton's theory of a universal vacuum — Perpetual motion — Cosmic magnetism — Kepler's ideas on cosmic forces — The cause of planetary rotation.

### SECTION 4—THE THEORIES OF ROTATION IN SCIENCE . . . . 224
Theories on how rotation began, and on the origin of planets and comets — The contradictions <note>original: "Paradoxes"</note> of science — Forces are real entities.

### SECTION 5—THE MASKS OF SCIENCE . . . 231
Physics or the study of reality beyond the physical <note>original: "Metaphysics"</note>? — Hidden doctrines and principles in the work of Spiller — Scientific definitions of force — The relationship between force and substance in the hidden sciences — What is force? — Practitioners of the hidden sciences call the cause of light, heat, sound, attraction <note>original: "Cohesion"</note>, and magnetism a substance — The seven mystic rays of the Sun — Causes and their effects — What is an atom? — The forty-nine original fires personified; their relationship to human mental <note>original: "Psychic"</note> faculties and chemical and physical powers — The "undifferentiated principle" <note>original: "Indiscrete Principle"</note> in the Qualified Non-Dualism <note>original: "Vishishtâdvaita"</note> system of Hindu philosophy.

### SECTION 12—SCIENTIFIC AND ESOTERIC EVIDENCE FOR, AND OBJECTIONS TO, THE MODERN NEBULAR THEORY . . . 312

## SECTION 1

### SYMBOLISM AND IDEOGRAPHS

> For is a symbol not always—to those who have the eyes to see it—some faint or clear revelation of the Divine? Through all things, there glimmers something of a Divine Idea. Indeed, the highest banner <term>ensign: a flag or standard indicating a particular group or idea</term> that men ever gathered and united under—the Cross itself—had no meaning, except for an accidental, external one.

> ->CARLYLE, *Sartor Resartus*<-

The study of the hidden meaning within every religious and secular <term>profane: here meaning non-religious or worldly legends</term> legend of every nation, large or small—and especially the traditions of the East—has occupied the greater part of this author's life. I am convinced that no mythological story or traditional event in a people's folklore has ever been pure fiction. Instead, every one of these narratives has a basis in actual history. 

In this regard, I disagree with those symbologists—regardless of how great their reputations may be—who find nothing in myths except further proof of the superstitious nature of the ancients. These scholars believe all mythologies originated from and are built upon "solar myths" <note>Solar myths: A popular 19th-century academic theory suggesting that all ancient myths were originally allegories describing the movements of the sun.</note>. These superficial thinkers have been expertly refuted by the poet and Egyptologist Mr. Gerald Massey in his lecture, "Moon-Worship <note>original: "Luniolatry"</note>, Ancient and Modern." His sharp criticism is worth repeating in this part of our work, as it reflects the feelings I expressed openly as far back as 1875, when my book *Isis Unveiled* was written.

For the past thirty years, Professor Max Müller has been teaching—in his books, lectures, and articles in the *Times*, *Saturday Review*, and various magazines, as well as from the platform of the Royal Institution and the pulpit of Westminster Abbey—that mythology is a "disease of language." He argues that ancient symbolism was the result of something like a primitive mental disorder <term>aberration: a departure from what is normal or right; a mental lapse</term>.

# THE SECRET DOCTRINE

“We know,” says Renouf <note>Sir Peter le Page Renouf (1822–1897), an influential English Egyptologist.</note>, echoing Max Müller <note>Friedrich Max Müller (1823–1900), a famous philologist who argued that myths were a "disease of language" caused by people forgetting the original meanings of words.</note> in his Hibbert lectures, “we know that mythology *is* the disease which springs up at a particular stage of human culture.” Such is the shallow explanation of those who do not believe in evolution, and such explanations are still accepted by the British public, which prefers to have its thinking done for it by others. Professor Max Müller, Cox, Gubernatis, and other proponents of the Solar Myth <note>The "Solar Myth" theory was a popular 19th-century belief that all ancient myths were originally allegories describing the movements of the sun.</note> have portrayed the primitive myth-maker as a sort of German-influenced Hindu philosopher, projecting his own mental shadows onto a mist and talking cleverly about smoke—or at least *clouds*—while the sky overhead becomes like a dream-land scribbled over with the imagery of prehistoric nightmares!

They imagine early man in their own likeness and view him as being perversely prone to confusing himself, or, as Fontenelle <note>Bernard le Bovier de Fontenelle (1657–1757), a French writer who explored the origins of myths.</note> puts it, “subject to seeing things that are not there!” They have misrepresented primitive or ancient man as having been idiotically misled from the start by an active but uneducated imagination into believing all sorts of fallacies. These fallacies would have been directly and constantly contradicted by his own daily experience. They treat him like a fool of his own fancy in the midst of the grim realities that were carving experiences into him, much like grinding icebergs leave their marks upon the rocks submerged beneath the sea. It remains to be said—and will one day be acknowledged—that these accepted teachers have been no closer to the beginnings of mythology and language than the poet Willie in Burns's poem was to Pegasus <note>Pegasus: the winged horse of Greek mythology representing poetic inspiration.</note>. 

My reply is this: it is nothing but the dream of a theoretical philosopher to suggest that mythology was a disease of language, or of anything else except his own brain. The origin and meaning of mythology have been missed entirely by these "solar-myth theorists" and weather-watchers! Mythology was a primitive way of *thinking* early thoughts. It was founded on natural facts and can still be verified by observing natural phenomena. There is nothing insane or irrational in it when viewed through the lens of evolution and when its method of expression—using sign-language—is thoroughly understood. The insanity lies in mistaking mythology for human history or Divine Revelation.¹ Mythology is the storehouse of man’s most ancient science, and what concerns us most is this: when it is truly interpreted once again, it is destined to be the end of those false theologies to which it has unintentionally given birth!²

In modern language, a statement is sometimes called "mythical" if it is untrue, but ancient mythology was not a system or method of lying in that sense. Its fables were the means of communicating facts; they were neither forgeries nor fictions. For example, when the Egyptians depicted the moon as a cat, they were not so ignorant that they supposed the moon was actually a cat, nor did their wandering imaginations see a physical likeness between the moon and a cat. A "cat-myth" was not just a flowery metaphor, nor did they intend to create puzzles or riddles. They had simply observed the fact that the cat sees in the dark and that its eyes become full circles and grow most luminous at night. 

The moon was the "seer" by night in the heavens, and the cat was its equivalent on earth; thus, the familiar cat was adopted as a representative—a natural sign, a living pictograph of the lunar orb. Following this logic, the sun, which "saw" down in the underworld at night, could also be called a cat (as it was), because it *also saw* in the dark. The name for a cat in Egyptian is *mau*, which means "the seer," derived from *mau*, "to see." One writer on mythology claims that the Egyptians “imagined a great cat behind the sun, and the sun is the pupil of the cat’s eye.” But this "imagining" is entirely a modern invention. It is the typical nonsense of the Müller school. The moon, acting as a cat, *was* the eye of the sun, *because it reflected*—

Selenography <term>the scientific study of the moon's physical features</term>, however, is the least esoteric <note>original: "esoteric" — intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with specialized knowledge.</note> of the divisions of lunar symbolism. The Moon is intimately related to the Earth, as shown in Stanza 6, Volume 1, and is more directly concerned with all the mysteries of our globe than even Venus-Lucifer—the Earth's occult sister and other self <note>original: alter ego</note>.¹

The tireless research of Western symbologists, especially Germans, during the last and present centuries, has led even the most open-minded students—and, of course, every occultist—to see that without the help of symbology, no ancient Scripture can ever be correctly understood. Symbology consists of seven departments, of which modern scholars know nothing. It must be studied from every possible angle, for each nation had its own unique methods of expression. In short, no Egyptian papyrus, no Indian palm-leaf manuscript <note>original: olla</note>,² no Assyrian tile, and no Hebrew scroll should be read and interpreted *literally*.

Every scholar now knows this. The capable lectures of Mr. Gerald Massey <note>Gerald Massey (1828–1907) was an English poet and self-taught Egyptologist who argued that Christian myths were derived from Egyptian ones.</note> alone are enough to convince any fair-minded Christian that accepting the literal meaning <note>original: "dead-letter"</note> of the *Bible* is equivalent to falling into a deeper error and superstition than any ever developed by the minds of the most "primitive" peoples. But there is a fact that even the most truth-seeking Orientalists—whether they study Aryan or Egyptian history—seem to remain blind to: every symbol on a papyrus or palm-leaf is a many-faced diamond. Each of these facets not only includes several interpretations but also relates to several different sciences. This is shown in the interpretation quoted above of the cat symbolizing the moon—an example of starry-earthly <note>original: "sidereo-terrestrial"</note> imagery—because for other nations, the moon has many other meanings as well.

As the late Kenneth Mackenzie—a learned Mason and Theosophist—showed in his *Royal Masonic Cyclopedia*, there is a great difference between an *emblem* and a *symbol*. An emblem "contains a larger series of thoughts than a symbol, which might be said to illustrate only one specific idea." Therefore, the symbols of several countries—lunar or solar symbols, for example—each illustrating such a specific idea or series of ideas, collectively form an esoteric emblem. An emblem is "a concrete, visible picture or sign representing principles, or a series of principles, recognizable by those who have received certain..."

# SYMBOLISM AND IDEOGRAPHS

The world and its human and animal races are discussed as thoroughly as I am able to treat them.

The evidence supporting these ancient teachings is scattered throughout the scriptures of ancient civilizations. The *Purânas* <note>Ancient Hindu texts containing myths, history, and philosophy.</note>, the *Zend Avesta* <note>The primary collection of religious texts of Zoroastrianism.</note>, and the old classics are full of such facts; however, no one has ever taken the trouble to collect and compare them. The reason for this is that all such events were recorded symbolically. Even the best scholars and the most sharp-minded *Âryanists* <note>19th-century scholars who studied the Indo-European (then called "Aryan") languages and cultures.</note> and *Egyptologists* <note>Scholars who study ancient Egyptian history and language.</note> have often been blinded by their own preconceived ideas and one-sided views of the secret meaning. 

Yet even a parable is a spoken symbol—a fiction or a fable, as some think—but we call it an allegorical representation of life's realities, events, and facts. Just as a moral was always drawn from a parable (a moral that represents an actual truth in human life), so too were real historical events deduced by those trained in the sacred <note>original: "hieratic"</note> sciences from the emblems and symbols recorded in ancient temple archives. The religious and secret history of every nation was embedded in symbols; it was never expressed literally in plain words. All the thoughts, emotions, and knowledge—both revealed by divine sources and acquired by humans—of the early races found their pictorial expression in allegory and parable. 

Why was this? Because *the spoken word has a power that is not only unknown to modern "wise men," but even suspected and naturally disbelieved by them. This is because sound and rhythm are closely related to the four Elements of the Ancients, and because specific vibrations in the air are sure to awaken corresponding Powers. Connecting with these Powers produces good or bad results, depending on the situation.* 

No student was ever allowed to recite historical, religious, or real events in plain, unmistakable words, for fear that the Powers connected with those events would be attracted once again. Such events were narrated only during Initiation <note>The process of being admitted into a secret society or receiving sacred knowledge.</note>, and every student had to record them using symbols drawn from their own mind. These were later examined by their Master before being finally accepted. In this way, the Chinese writing system was gradually created, just as the sacred symbols were established in ancient Egypt shortly before. In the Chinese language—the characters of which can be read in any language¹ and which is only slightly less ancient than the Egyptian alphabet of Thoth <note>The ancient Egyptian god of wisdom, writing, and magic.</note>—every word has a corresponding symbol in pictorial form. This language possesses many thousands of such symbol-letters, or logograms <term>signs or characters representing a whole word or phrase</term>, each conveying the meaning of an entire word. This is because they do not use letters or an alphabet as we understand them.

The author discovered that this geometrical ratio [the whole-number ratio of the diameter to the circumference of a circle, known as Pi] was the very ancient, and probably the divine, origin of linear measures. > To clear up any confusion regarding the term "language": Primarily, the word means the expression of ideas through human speech, but secondarily, it may mean the expression of ideas through any other method. # SYMBOLISM AND IDEOGRAPHS

In human civilization, a picture of a natural object may give rise to a set of related ideas. These ideas radiate outward in various and even opposing directions—like the spokes of a wheel—producing natural realities in fields of study that seem very foreign to the initial subject of the starting picture. One notion may lead to another connected notion; if so, then no matter how unrelated they appear, all resulting ideas must spring from the original picture and be harmoniously linked to one another. 

If the initial pictured idea is fundamental enough, it could result in a complete understanding of the cosmos, even in its structural details. Such a use of language is now obsolete. However, the writer has begun to wonder whether, in the distant past, this system—or something like it—was once the universal language of the world. As it became more complex and took on <term>arcane</term> <note>original: "arcane"; secret, mysterious, or understood by only a few initiates.</note> forms, it was likely guarded by a select class or caste. By this, I mean that the common speech—the <term>vernacular</term>—began to be used as a vehicle for this peculiar mode of conveying ideas. The evidence for this is very strong. Indeed, it seems that in the history of the human race, there was a decline or loss of an original, perfect language and a perfect system of science. Should we say they were "perfect" because they were of divine origin and introduction?¹

In this context, "Divine origin" does not mean a revelation from an <term>anthropomorphic</term> <note>Having human characteristics; imagining a god with a human form and personality.</note> God on a mountain amidst thunder and lightning. Instead, as we understand it, it refers to a language and a system of science taught to early mankind by a more advanced *mankind*. This group was so much higher that they appeared *divine* in the sight of those infant humans. In short, they were a "mankind" from other spheres. This idea contains nothing supernatural; its acceptance or rejection depends simply on the level of conceit and arrogance in the mind of the person hearing it. 

If the professors of modern knowledge would only admit that—even though they know nothing of the future of the soul (or rather, refuse to accept anything)—that future might be full of surprises and unexpected revelations once their **Egos** <note>In Theosophical terms, the "Ego" refers to the permanent spiritual self or soul that reincarnates across many lifetimes.</note> are rid of their heavy physical bodies, then materialistic disbelief would have fewer ground to stand on. Who among them knows, or can say, what may happen once the Life-Cycle of this globe is finished and our mother Earth herself falls into her last sleep? Who is bold enough to say that the *divine Egos* of our humanity—at least the chosen few among the multitudes passing on to other worlds—*will not become in their turn* the "divine" instructors of a new humanity? This new race would be generated by them on a new globe, called to life and activity by the spiritual principles of our own Earth. All of this may have been the experience of the PAST, and these strange records lie embedded in the "Mystery Language" of prehistoric ages—the language now called SYMBOLISM.

THE SECRET DOCTRINE

Proposition IX is a remarkable example of faulty reasoning, though it is the one on which Mr. Parker’s *Quadrature* <note>*Quadrature of the Circle*, by John A. Parker, pp. 117-9, 1851.</note> mainly rests. It states that:

The circle and the equilateral triangle are opposite to one another in all the elements of their construction, and hence the fractional diameter of one circle, which is equal to the diameter of one square, is in the opposite duplicate ratio to the diameter of an equilateral triangle whose area is one, etc., etc.

Even if we grant, for the sake of argument, that a triangle can be said to have a radius in the sense in which we speak of the radius of a circle—for what Parker calls the radius of the triangle is actually the radius of a circle inscribed within a triangle, and therefore not the radius of the triangle at all—and even if we grant for the moment the other fanciful mathematical propositions united in his premises, why must we conclude that, if the equilateral triangle and circle are opposite in all elements of their construction, the diameter of any defined circle is in the opposite duplicate ratio of the diameter of any given equivalent triangle? What necessary connection is there between the premises and the conclusion? This reasoning is of a kind unknown in geometry and would not be accepted by strict mathematicians.

Whether the ancient Esoteric system originated the British inch or not is of little consequence, however, to the strict and true metaphysician. Nor does Mr. Ralston Skinner’s esoteric reading of the *Bible* become incorrect merely because the measurements of the Pyramid may not be found to agree with those of Solomon’s Temple, Noah’s Ark, etc., or because Mr. Parker’s Quadrature of the Circle is rejected by mathematicians. For Mr. Skinner’s reading depends primarily on the Kabbalistic methods and the Rabbinical value of the Hebrew letters. But it is extremely important to determine whether the measures used in the evolution of the symbolic religion of the Aryans—in the construction of their temples, in the figures given in the *Puranas*, and especially in their chronology, their astronomical symbols, the duration of cycles, and other computations—were or were not the same as those used in Biblical measurements and glyphs. For this would prove that the Jews, unless they took their sacred cubit and measurements from the Egyptians—Moses being an Initiate of their Priests—must have obtained those notions from India. ## PRIMORDIAL SUBSTANCE AND DIVINE THOUGHT

> As it would seem irrational to claim that we already know all existing causes, permission must be granted to assume an entirely new agent if necessary. . . .
>
> Assuming what is not yet strictly accurate—that the undulatory hypothesis accounts for all the facts—we are called upon to decide whether the existence of an undulating ether is thereby proved. We cannot positively affirm that no other supposition will explain the facts. Newton's corpuscular hypothesis is admitted to have broken down on Interference, and there is at the present day no rival. Still, it is extremely desirable in all such hypotheses to find some collateral confirmation, some evidence *aliunde* <note>from elsewhere</note> of the supposed Ether. Some hypotheses consist of assumptions regarding the minute structure and operations of bodies. From the nature of the case, these assumptions can never be proved by direct means. Their only merit is their suitability to express the phenomena. They are Representative Fictions.

->Logic, by Alexander Bain, LL.D., Part II, pp. 131-2 (1873)<-

ETHER—this hypothetical Proteus, one of the “representative fictions” of modern Science, which was nevertheless accepted for so long—is one of the lower “principles” of what we call Primordial Substance (Âkâsha, in Sanskrit). It is one of the dreams of old, which has now again become the dream of modern Science. It is the greatest, as it is the boldest, of the surviving speculations of ancient philosophers. For the Occultists, however, both ETHER and the Primordial Substance are realities. To put it plainly, ETHER is the Astral Light, and the Primordial Substance is ÂKÂSHA, the UPÂDHI <note>the basis or vehicle</note> of DIVINE THOUGHT.

In modern language, the latter would be better named COSMIC IDEATION (Spirit), and the former, COSMIC SUBSTANCE (Matter). These, the Alpha and the Omega of Being, are but the two *facets* of the one Absolute Existence. This Absolute Existence was never addressed, or even mentioned, by any name in antiquity, except in allegory. In the oldest Aryan race, the Hindu, the worship of the intellectual classes never consisted of an adoration of marvelous form and art, however fervent, as it did with the Greeks; an adoration which led later on to anthropomorphism. But while the Greek philosopher adored form, and the Hindu sage alone “perceived the true relation of earthly beauty and eternal truth”—the uneducated of every nation understood neither, at any time.

The philosophers themselves had to be *initiated into the mysteries of perception* before they could grasp the correct idea of the Ancients regarding this most metaphysical subject. Otherwise—without such Initiation—every thinker faces a limit of “this far shall you go and no further,” determined by his own intellectual capacity. This limit is as clear and unmistakable as the one set for the progress of any nation or race in its cycle by the law of <term>Karma</term>. The ideals of each are only the necessary results of their temperaments and the outcome of that phase of intellectual progress which a nation, as a whole, has attained. It will be an easy task to show that cosmogonical legends all over the world are based on the knowledge the ancients had of those sciences which, in our day, have joined together in support of the doctrine of evolution; and that further research may demonstrate that these ancients were far better acquainted with the fact of evolution itself—embracing both its physical and spiritual aspects—than we are now.

With the old philosophers, evolution was a universal theorem, a doctrine embracing the *whole*, and an established principle, whereas our modern evolutionists can only present us with speculative theories—with *particular*, if not entirely *negative* theorems. # SECTION 4

## CHAOS : THEOS : KOSMOS

THESE three are the containment of Space; or, as a learned Kabalist has defined it: "Space, the all-containing uncontained, is the primary embodiment of simple unity . . . boundless extension."¹ But, he asks again, "Boundless extension of what?"—and makes the correct reply: "*the unknown container of all, space, the unknown first Cause.*" This is a most correct definition and answer; most esoteric and true, from every aspect of Occult Teaching.

Space, which modern wiseacres—in their ignorance and with their iconoclastic tendency to destroy every philosophical idea of old—have proclaimed "an abstract idea" and a *void*, is, in reality, the Container and *the body of the Universe* in its seven principles. It is a body of limitless extent, whose PRINCIPLES, in Occult phraseology—each being in its turn a septenary—manifest in our phenomenal World only the grossest fabric of *their subdivisions*. "No one has ever seen the Elements in their fullness," the DOCTRINE teaches. We have to search for our Wisdom in the original expressions and synonyms of the primeval peoples. Even the Jews, the latest of these, show the same idea in their Kabalistic teachings when they speak of the seven-headed Serpent of Space, called "the great Sea."

> In the beginning, the Alhim created the Heavens and the Earth, the Six [Sephiroth]. They created Six, and on these all things are based. And these [Six] depend upon the *seven forms of the Cranium up to the Dignity of all Dignities*.²

Now *Wind*, *Air*, and *Spirit* have always been synonymous in every nation. Pneuma (Spirit) and Anemos (Wind) among the Greeks, and *Spiritus* and *Ventus* among the Latins, were interchangeable terms, even if dissociated from the original idea of the Breath of Life. In the "Forces" of Science, we see only the material effect of the spiritual effect of one or another of the four primordial Elements, transmitted to us by the Fourth Race just as we shall transmit Ether—or rather its gross subdivision—in its fullness to the Sixth Root-Race.

# CHAOS : THEOS : KOSMOS

"Chaos" was called senseless by the Ancients because—since Chaos and Space are synonymous—it represented and contained within itself all the Elements in their rudimentary, undifferentiated state. They made Ether, the fifth Element, the synthesis of the other four; for the Ether of the Greek philosophers was not its residue, although they certainly knew more than modern science does about these remnants, which are rightly enough supposed to act as an agent for many forces that manifest on Earth. Their Ether was the Âkâsha of the Hindus; the Ether accepted in modern Physics is but one of its sub-divisions on our plane—the *Astral Light* of the Kabbalists, with all its evil as well as its good effects.

Seeing that the essence of Ether, or Unseen Space, was considered divine—as the supposed Veil of Deity—it was regarded as the medium between this life and the next. The Ancients believed that when the directing, active Intelligences—the Gods—retired from any portion of Ether *in our Space*, or the four realms which they supervise, then that particular region was left in the possession of evil, so-called because of the absence of Good.

The existence of Spirit in the common mediator, the Ether, is denied by Materialism, while Theology turns it into a Personal God. But the Kabbalist holds that both are wrong, saying that in Ether, the elements represent only Matter—the blind Cosmic Forces of Nature—while *Spirit* represents the Intelligence which directs them. The Aryan, Hermetic, Orphic, and Pythagorean cosmogonical doctrines, as well as those of Sanchuniathon and Berosus, are all based upon one irrefutable formula: that Ether and Chaos—or, in Platonic language, Mind and Matter—were the two primeval and eternal principles of the Universe, utterly independent of anything else. The former was the all-vivifying intellectual principle, while Chaos was a shapeless liquid principle, without "form or sense." From the union of these two, the Universe—or rather the Universal World—sprang into existence as the first Androgynous Deity: Chaotic Matter becoming its Body, and Ether its Soul. According to the phrasing of a fragment from Hermias: "Chaos, from this union with Spirit, obtaining sense, shone with pleasure, and thus was produced Protogonos (the First-Born) Light."¹ This is the universal Trinity, based on the metaphysical conceptions of the Ancients, who, reasoning by analogy, viewed man—who is a compound of Intellect and Matter—as the Microcosm of the Macrocosm, or Great Universe.²

"*Nature abhors a vacuum*," said the Peripatetics. Though they were materialists in their own way, they perhaps understood why Democritus, along with his instructor Leucippus, taught that the first principles of all things contained in the Universe were Atoms and a *vacuum*. This "vacuum" simply means *latent* Deity, or Force which—before its first manifestation, when it became WILL and gave the first impulse to these atoms—was the great *Nothingness*, Ain Soph, or NOTHING, and, therefore, to every sense, a Void or CHAOS.

The attempt to derive *God* from the Anglo-Saxon synonym *Good* is an abandoned idea, for in no other language, from the Persian *Khoda* down to the Latin *Deus*, has an instance been found of the name for *God* being derived from the attribute of goodness. To the Latin peoples, it comes from the Aryan *Dyaus* (the Day); to the Slavic, from the Greek *Bacchus* (*Bagh-bog*); and to the Saxon peoples directly from the Hebrew *Yod*, or *Jod*. The latter is י, the number-letter 10, male and female, and *Yod* is the phallic hook. Hence the Saxon *Godh*, the Germanic *Gott*, and the English *God*. This symbolic term may be said to represent the Creator of physical humanity on the terrestrial plane; but surely it had nothing to do with the formation or "creation" of either spirit, gods, or *kosmos*?

*Chaos-Theos-Kosmos*, the Triple Deity, is *all in all*. Therefore, it is said to be male and female, good and evil, positive and negative—the whole series of contrasted qualities. When latent, in <term>Pralaya</term>, it is unknowable and becomes the Unknowable Deity. It can be known only through its active functions; hence as Matter-Force and *living Spirit*—the correlations and outcome, or the expression on the visible plane of the ultimate and forever unknown Unity.

In turn, this Triple Unit is the producer of the four primary elements,¹ which are known in our visible terrestrial nature as the seven (so far only five) elements, each divisible into forty-nine—seven times seven—sub-elements, with about seventy of which chemistry is acquainted. Every cosmic element, such as fire, air, water, and earth, partaking of the qualities and defects of its primaries, is in its nature good and evil, force or spirit, and matter, etc. Therefore, each is at one and the same time life and death, health and disease, action and reaction. They are ever forming matter under the never-ceasing impulse of the One Element, the Unknowable, represented in the world of phenomena by Ether. They are "the immortal gods who give birth and life to all."

The Hindus have an endless series of allegories to express this idea. In the Primordial Chaos, before it developed into the <term>Sapta Samudra</term> (Seven Oceans)—emblematic of the Seven <term>Gunas</term> or conditioned Qualities, composed of the <term>Trigunas</term> (<term>Sattva</term>, <term>Rajas</term>, and <term>Tamas</term>)—both <term>Amrita</term> (Immortality) and <term>Visha</term> (Poison, Death, Evil) lie latent. This is found in the allegorical Churning of the Ocean by the Gods. <term>Amrita</term> is beyond any <term>Guna</term>, for it is *unconditioned in itself*; but once it fell into phenomenal creation, it became mixed with Evil—Chaos with latent <term>Theos</term> in it—before the Kosmos was evolved. Hence we find Vishnu, the personification of Eternal Law, periodically calling the Kosmos into activity; or, in allegorical phrasing, churning the <term>Amrita</term> of Eternity out of the Primitive Ocean or Boundless Chaos, which is reserved only for the Gods and <term>Devas</term>. In this task, he must employ <term>Nâgas</term> and <term>Asuras</term>, or Demons in exoteric Hinduism. The whole allegory is highly philosophical, and indeed we find it repeated in every ancient system of philosophy. Thus we find it in Plato, who, having fully embraced the ideas which Pythagoras had brought from India, compiled and published them in a form more intelligible than the original mysterious numerals of the Greek Sage. Thus, for Plato, the Kosmos is the “Son,” having Divine Thought and Matter as his Father and Mother.²

> “The Egyptians,” says Dunlap, “distinguished between an Older and Younger Horus; the former was the *brother* of Osiris; the latter the *Son* of Osiris and Isis.”³ The first is the Idea of the World remaining in the Demiurgic Mind, “born in Darkness before the Creation of the World.” The second Horus is this “Idea” going forth from the <term>Logos</term>, becoming clothed with matter, and assuming an actual existence.⁴

> The *Chaldean Oracles* speak of the “Mundane God, eternal, boundless, young and old, of winding form.”⁵ This “winding form” is a figure used to express the vibratory motion of the Astral Light, with which the ancient priests were perfectly well acquainted, even though the name “Astral Light” was invented by the Martinists.

# SECTION 5

## ON THE HIDDEN DEITY, ITS SYMBOLS AND GLYPHS

The Logos, or Creative Deity, the “Word made Flesh” of every religion, must be traced back to its ultimate source and essence. In India, it is a Proteus of 1,008 divine names and aspects in each of its *personal transformations*, from Brahmâ-Purusha, through the Seven *divine* Rishis and Ten *Semi-divine* Prajâpatis (also Rishis), down to the *divine-human* Avatâras. The same puzzling problem of the “One in many” and the multitude in One is found in other pantheons; in the Egyptian, the Greek, and the Chaldeo-Judaic. The latter has made the confusion even more confused by presenting its Gods as euhemerizations in the forms of patriarchs. And these patriarchs are now accepted as living and historical entities by those who reject Romulus as a myth. *Verbum satis sapienti!* <note>A word to the wise is sufficient!</note>

In the *Zohar*, Ain Soph is also the One, the Infinite Unity. This was known to the very few learned Fathers of the Church who were aware that Jehovah was not the “highest” God, but a *third-rate potency*. But while complaining bitterly about the Gnostics and saying, “our heretics hold . . . that PROPATÔR is known only to the ONLY-BEGOTTEN son¹ <gloss>who is Brahmâ</gloss>, that is, to the Mind <gloss>*Nous*</gloss>,” Irenæus failed to mention that the Jews did the same in their actual secret books. Valentinus, “the most profound doctor of the Gnosis,” held that “there was a perfect AIÔN who existed before Bythos <gloss>the first Father of unfathomable nature, which is the Second Logos</gloss>, called Propatôr.” It is this AIÔN who springs like a ray from Ain Soph, who *does not create*, and the AIÔN who creates, or rather *through* whom everything is created or evolves. For, as the Basilidians taught, “there was a Supreme God, Abrasax, by whom was created Mind <gloss>*Mahat* in Sanskrit, *Nous* in Greek</gloss>. From Mind proceeded the Word, *Logos*; from the Word came Providence <gloss>or rather, Divine Light</gloss>; then from it came Virtue and Wisdom in Principalities, Powers,

Here, then, we find the same system as in the *Puranas*, in which the Incomprehensible drops a Seed, which becomes the Golden Egg, from which Brahma is produced. Brahma produces Mahat, etc. True Esoteric Philosophy, however, speaks neither of "creation" nor of "evolution" in the sense that external religions do. All these personified Powers are not evolutions from one another, but various aspects of the single and sole manifestation of the ABSOLUTE ALL.

The same system as that of the Gnostic Emanations prevails in the Sephirothic aspects of Ain Soph, and, as *these aspects exist in Space and Time*, a certain order is maintained in their successive appearances. Therefore, it becomes impossible not to notice the great changes that the *Zohar* has undergone through the handling of generations of Christian Mystics. For even in the metaphysics of the *Talmud*, the "Lower Face" or "Lesser Countenance," or Microprosopus, could never be placed on the same level of abstract ideals as the Higher, or "Greater Countenance," Macroprosopus. In the Chaldean *Kabbalah*, the latter is a pure abstraction: the Word, or LOGOS, or DABAR in Hebrew. This Word—though it actually becomes a plural number, or "Words," D(a)B(a)R(i)M, when it reflects itself or takes the form of a Host (of Angels or Sephiroth, meaning "Number")—is still collectively ONE, and on the ideal plane, it is a zero, ◯, "No-thing." It is without form or being, "with no likeness to anything else."¹ And even Philo calls the Creator—the LOGOS who stands next to God—the "SECOND GOD" when he speaks of "the Second God, who is his [the Highest God’s] WISDOM."² Deity is not God. It is NOTHING and DARKNESS. It is nameless, and therefore called Ain Soph, the word "Ayin" meaning "nothing."³ The "Highest God," the Unmanifested Logos, is Its Son.

Nor are most of the Gnostic systems that have come down to us—mutilated as they are by the Church Fathers—anything better than the distorted shells of the original speculations. Moreover, they were never open to the public or the general reader; for if their hidden meaning or esotericism had been revealed, it would no longer have been an esoteric teaching, and this could never have happened. In his *Revelation*, speaking of divine mysteries expressed through letters and numbers, Marcus recounts how the "Supreme Tetrad came down" to him "from the region that cannot be seen or named, in a female form, because the world would have been unable to endure her appearing in a male figure," and revealed to him "the generation of the universe, never before told to either Gods or men."

The first sentence already contains a double meaning. Why should the appearance of a female figure be more easily endured or listened to by the world than a male figure? On the face of it, this appears nonsensical. But to one who is acquainted with the *Mystery Language*, it is quite clear and simple. *Esoteric Philosophy*, or the *Secret Wisdom*, was symbolized by a female form, while a male figure stood for the *Unveiled Mystery*. When <term>Theosophists</term> and <term>Occultists</term> say that God is not a BEING, because IT is No-thing (NO-THING), they are more reverent and religiously respectful to the Deity than those who call God "HE," and thus make Him into a gigantic MALE.

Whoever studies the <term>Kabbalah</term> will soon find the same idea in the ultimate thought of its authors—the earlier and great Hebrew Initiates—who obtained this Secret Wisdom in Babylonia from the Chaldean <term>Hierophants</term>, just as Moses obtained his in Egypt. The <term>Zoharic</term> system cannot easily be judged by its later translations into Latin and other languages, where all its ideas were softened to fit the views and policies of its Christian editors; for its original ideas are identical to those of all other religious systems. The various <term>Cosmogonies</term> show that the *Universal Soul*³ was considered by every ancient nation to be the "Mind" of the <term>Demiurgic Creator</term>. It was called the Mother, <term>Sophia</term> (or female Wisdom) by the <term>Gnostics</term>; <term>Sephira</term> by the Jews; and <term>Sarasvatî</term> or <term>Vâch</term> by the Hindus. The <term>Holy Ghost</term> was also considered a female Principle.

# THE SECRET DOCTRINE

<term>Anu</term> in Sanskrit means "atom," *aniyâmsam-aniyâsâm* (the smallest of the small), being a name of <term>Parabrahman</term> in the <term>Vedântic</term> philosophy. # SECTION 6

## THE MUNDANE EGG

Where does this universal symbol originate? The Egg was incorporated as a sacred sign in the <term>Cosmogony</term> of every people on Earth, and was revered both for its form and its inner mystery. From humanity’s earliest mental concepts, it has been known as the symbol that most successfully represented the origin and secret of Being. The gradual development of the imperceptible germ within the closed shell; the internal process—occurring without any apparent outside force—which produced an active *something* from a hidden *nothing*, requiring only heat; and which, after evolving into a tangible, living creature, broke its shell to appear to everyone's senses as a self-generated and self-created being—all this must have been a constant miracle from the beginning.

The Secret Teaching explains the reason for this reverence through the symbolism of prehistoric races. In the beginning, the "<term>First Cause</term>" had no name. Later, thinkers imagined it as an eternally invisible, mysterious Bird that dropped an Egg into Chaos, and this Egg became the Universe. Thus, <term>Brahmâ</term> was called <term>Kâlahamsa</term>, the "Swan in [Space and] Time." Becoming the "Swan of Eternity," <term>Brahmâ</term> lays a Golden Egg at the start of each <term>Mahâmanvantara</term>; this egg represents the great Circle (or <image-desc>small circle symbol</image-desc>), which is itself a symbol for the Universe and its spherical bodies.

A second reason the Egg was chosen as the symbolic representation of the Universe and our Earth was its shape. It was both a circle and a sphere, and the egg-like shape of our globe must have been known from the very beginning of symbology, since it was so universally adopted. The belief that the <term>Kosmos</term> first manifested in the form of an Egg was the most widespread view in antiquity. As Bryant shows,<note>¹ *An Analysis of Ancient Mythology*, Vol. iii, p. 165.</note> it was a symbol adopted by the Greeks, Syrians, Persians, and Egyptians. In the <term>Egyptian Ritual</term>, <term>Seb</term> (the God of Time and Earth) is described as having laid an

# THE SECRET DOCTRINE

In view of this circular form—the "1" issuing from the O, or the Egg, or the male from the female in the androgyne—it is strange to find a scholar saying, on the grounds that the most ancient Indian manuscripts show no trace of it, that the ancient <term>Âryans</term> were ignorant of <term>decimal notation</term>. The 10, being the sacred number of the Universe, was secret and esoteric, regarding both the unit and the cipher, or zero, the circle. Moreover, Professor Max Muller tells us that "the two words *cipher and zero*, which are but one, are sufficient to prove that our figures are borrowed from the Arabs."¹ Cipher is the Arabic *cifron*, and means "empty," a translation of the Sanskrit *shûnyam*, or "naught," says the Professor.² The Arabs got their figures from Hindustân, and never claimed the discovery for themselves. As for the Pythagoreans, we need only turn to the ancient manuscripts of Boethius's treatise, *De Arithmetica*, composed in the sixth century, to find the "1" and the "0" among the Pythagorean numerals as the first and final figures.³ And Porphyry, who quotes from the Pythagorean Moderatus,⁴ says that the numerals of Pythagoras were "hieroglyphical symbols, by means of which he explained ideas concerning the nature of things," or the origin of the Universe.

Now, if on the one hand the most ancient Indian manuscripts show as yet no trace of decimal notation in them, and Max Muller states very clearly that until now he has found but nine letters, the initials of the Sanskrit numerals; on the other hand, we have records just as ancient to provide the needed proof. We speak of the sculptures and the sacred imagery in the most ancient temples of the Far East. Pythagoras derived his knowledge from India, and we find Professor Max Muller corroborating this statement, at least so far as to allow that the Neo-Pythagoreans were the first teachers of "*ciphering*" among the Greeks and Romans; that they "at Alexandria, or in Syria, became acquainted with the Indian figures, and adapted them to the Pythagorean Abacus (our figures)." This cautious admission implies that Pythagoras himself was acquainted with only *nine* figures. Thus we might reasonably answer that, although we possess no certain proof, exoterically, that the decimal notation was known to Pythagoras, who lived at the very close of the archaic ages,⁵ yet we have sufficient evidence to show that the full numbers, as given by Boethius, were known to the Pythagoreans, even

The symbolism of the Lunar and Solar Deities is so inextricably mixed that it is almost impossible to separate such symbols as the Egg, the Lotus, and the "Sacred" Animals from each other. The *Ibis*, for example, was held in the greatest veneration in Egypt. It was sacred to Isis, who is often represented with the head of that bird, and also sacred to Mercury or Thoth, who is said to have assumed its form while escaping from Typhon. Herodotus <note>*Euterpe* (Book II of *The Histories*)</note> tells us there were two kinds of ibises in Egypt: one *entirely black*, the other black and white. The former is credited with fighting and exterminating the winged serpents that came from Arabia every spring and infested the country. The other was sacred to the Moon because that celestial body is white and brilliant on its outer side, yet dark and black on the side it never turns toward the Earth. Moreover, the ibis kills land serpents and wreaks terrible havoc among the eggs of the crocodile, thereby saving Egypt from having the Nile over-infested by those horrible reptiles. The bird is credited with doing this in the moonlight, thus being aided by Isis, whose stellar symbol is the Moon. But the more accurate esoteric truth underlying these popular myths is that Hermes—as shown by Abenephius <note>*On Egyptian Worship*</note>—watched over the Egyptians in the form of that bird and taught them the occult arts and sciences. This simply means that the *ibis religiosa* had, and has, "magical" properties in common with many other birds—preeminently the albatross and the mythical white swan, the Swan of Eternity or Time, the <term>KÂLAHANSA</term>.

### SECTION 7

## THE DAYS AND NIGHTS OF BRAHMÂ

THIS is the name given to the periods called <term>MANVANTARA</term> (<term>MANU-ANTARA</term>, or between the Manus) and <term>PRALAYA</term>, or Dissolution; one referring to the active periods of the Universe, the other to its times of relative and complete rest, whether they occur at the end of a "Day" or an "Age" (a life) of <term>Brahmâ</term>. These periods, which follow each other in regular succession, are also called small and great <term>Kalpas</term>, the minor and the <term>Mahâ Kalpas</term>, though, properly speaking, the <term>Mahâ Kalpa</term> is never a "day," but a whole life or age of <term>Brahmâ</term>; for it is said in the *Brahma Vaivarta*: "Chronologers compute a <term>Kalpa</term> by the Life of <term>Brahmâ</term>. Minor <term>Kalpas</term>, such as <term>Samvarta</term> and the rest, are numerous." In sober truth, they are infinite, for they have never had a beginning; or, in other words, there never was a *first* <term>Kalpa</term>, nor will there ever be a *last*, in Eternity.

One <term>Parârdha</term>, or half of the existence of <term>Brahmâ</term>, in the ordinary understanding of this measure of time, has already expired in the present <term>Mahâ Kalpa</term>; the last <term>Kalpa</term> was the <term>Padma</term>, or that of the Golden Lotus; the present one is the <term>Varâha</term>,<note>1</note> the "Boar" Incarnation, or <term>Avatâra</term>.

One thing is to be especially noted by the scholar who studies the Hindu religion from the <term>Puranâs</term>: he must not take the statements found there literally, and in one sense only; and especially those which concern

# THE DAYS AND NIGHTS OF BRAHMÂ

The <term>Manvantaras</term>, or <term>Kalpas</term>, must be understood in their various contexts. Thus, these periods refer, in the same terminology, to both the great and the small cycles—to <term>Mahâ Kalpas</term> and to minor <term>Cycles</term>. The <term>Matsya</term>, or Fish <term>Avatâra</term>, occurred before the <term>Varâha</term>, or Boar <term>Avatâra</term>; therefore, the allegories must relate to both the <term>Padma</term> and the present <term>Manvantara</term>, as well as to the minor cycles that have occurred since the reappearance of our Chain of Worlds and the Earth. Since the <term>Matsya Avatâra</term> of <term>Vishnu</term> and <term>Vaivasvata</term>’s Deluge are correctly connected with an event that happened on our Earth during this Round, it is evident that while it may relate to pre-cosmic events (in the sense of *our* <term>Kosmos</term>, or Solar System), in our case, it refers to a distant geological period. Not even <term>Esoteric Philosophy</term> can claim to know—except by analogical inference—what took place before the reappearance of our Solar System and prior to the last <term>Mahâ Pralaya</term>.

But it teaches clearly that after the first geological disturbance of the Earth’s axis—which ended in the entire second continent being swept to the bottom of the sea, along with its primeval races (of which successive continents or "Earths," <term>Atlantis</term> was the fourth)—there was another disturbance. This was caused by the axis again resuming its previous degree of inclination as rapidly as it had changed it, at which time the Earth was indeed *raised once more out of the waters*—as above, so below, and *vice versa*. Tradition says there were "Gods" on Earth in those days—Gods, and not men as we know them now.

As will be shown in Volume 3, the calculation of periods in exoteric <term>Hinduism</term> refers to both the great cosmic and the small terrestrial events and cataclysms, and the same can be shown regarding names. For example, the name <term>Yudhishthira</term>—the first king of the <term>Sacae</term> or <term>Shakas</term>, who begins the <term>Kali Yuga Era</term> (which is to last 432,000 years), an actual king who lived in 3,102 B.C.—applies, name and all, to the great Deluge at the time of the first sinking of <term>Atlantis</term>. He is the "<term>Yudhishthira</term>,<note>1</note> born on the mountain of the hundred peaks, at the edge of the world, *beyond which nobody can go*," and "immediately after the flood."<note>2</note> We know of no "Flood" in 3,102 B.C.—not even that of Noah—for according to <term>Judæo-Christian</term> chronology, it took place in 2,349 B.C.

Let us see, however, what the three kinds of <term>Pralayas</term> were, and what the *popular* belief is about them. For once, it agrees with Esotericism.

Of the <term>Pralaya</term> before which fourteen <term>Manvantaras</term> elapse—having over them as many presiding <term>Manus</term>, and at whose close the "incidental" or Brahmâ's Dissolution occurs—it is said in the <term>Vishnu Purâna</term>, in a condensed paraphrase:

> At the end of a thousand periods of four ages, which complete a day of Brahmâ, the earth is, for the most part, exhausted. The eternal (Avyaya) <term>Vishnu</term> then assumes the character of <term>Rudra</term>, the destroyer (<term>Shiva</term>), and descends to reunite all (his) creatures to himself. He enters into the seven rays of the sun, drinks up all the waters of the (Globe), and causes all moisture to evaporate; thus drying up the whole earth. The seas and rivers, the mountain torrents and springs, are all exhaled. Thus fed with abundant moisture, the seven solar rays dilate into seven suns and set the three worlds on fire. The destroyer of all things, <term>Hari</term>, who is the flame of time (<term>Kâlâgni</term>), [finally consumes the Earth]. Then <term>Rudra</term>, becoming <term>Janârdana</term>, breathes clouds and rain. <gloss>1</gloss>

There are many kinds of <term>Pralaya</term>, but three chief periods are specifically mentioned in old Hindu books. The first of these, as Wilson shows, is called <term>NAIMITTIKA</term>, <gloss>2</gloss> "occasional" or "incidental," caused by the intervals of "Brahmâ's Days"; it is the destruction of creatures—of all that lives and has a form—but not of the substance, which remains *in statu quo* until the new DAWN after that Night. The second is called <term>PRÂKRITIKA</term> and occurs at the end of the Age or Life of Brahmâ, when everything that exists is resolved into the Primal Element, to be remodeled at the end of that longer Night. The third, <term>Atyantika</term>, does not concern the Worlds or the Universe, but only the individualities of certain people. It is thus the individual <term>Pralaya</term>, or <term>NIRVÂNA</term>; once this is reached, no more future existence is possible—no rebirth until after the <term>Mahâ Pralaya</term>. This latter Night—lasting as it does 311,040,000,000,000 years, with the possibility also of being almost doubled in the case of the lucky <term>Jivanmukta</term> who reaches <term>Nirvâna</term> at an early period of a <term>Manvantara</term>—is long enough to be regarded as *eternal*, if not endless. # THE DAYS AND NIGHTS OF BRAHMÂ

The *Purâna* <sup>1</sup> speaks of a fourth kind of <term>Pralaya</term>, the *Nitya*, or constant dissolution, and explains it as the change that takes place imperceptibly in everything in this Universe, from the globe down to the atom, without ceasing. It is growth and decay—life and death.

When the <term>Mahâ Pralaya</term> arrives, the inhabitants of <term>Svar-loka</term> (the upper sphere), disturbed by the conflagration, seek refuge “with the <term>Pitris</term>, their progenitors, the <term>Manus</term>, the Seven <term>Rishis</term>, the various orders of celestial Spirits, and the Gods, in <term>Mahar-loka</term>.” When the latter is reached also, all the beings listed above migrate in their turn from <term>Mahar-loka</term> and travel to <term>Jana-loka</term>, “*in their subtle forms, destined to be re-embodied in capacities similar to their previous ones when the world is renewed at the beginning of the succeeding <term>Kalpa</term>.*” <sup>2</sup>

Clouds, mighty in size and loud with thunder, fill up all space <note><term>Nabhas-tala</term></note>. Showering down torrents of water, these clouds quench the dreadful fires        and then they rain uninterruptedly for a hundred [divine] years and deluge the whole world <note>Solar System</note>. Pouring down in drops as large as dice, these rains overspread the earth, fill the middle region (<term>Bhuva-loka</term>), and inundate heaven. The world is now enveloped in darkness, and all things, animate or inanimate, having perished, the clouds continue to pour down their waters,        <note>and the night of <term>Brahmâ</term> reigns supreme over the scene of desolation <sup>3</sup></note>.

This is what we call in the Esoteric Doctrine a Solar <term>Pralaya</term>. When the waters have reached the region of the Seven <term>Rishis</term> and the world, or Solar System, is one ocean, they stop. The breath of <term>Vishnu</term> becomes a strong wind, which blows for another hundred (divine) years until all clouds are dispersed. The wind is then reabsorbed, and THAT—

Of whom all things are made, the lord by whom all things exist, he who is inconceivable, without beginning, the beginning of the universe, reposes, sleeping upon <term>Shesha</term> <note>the Serpent of Infinity</note> in the midst of the deep. The creator <note>(?) <term>Âdikrit</term></note> <term>Hari</term> sleeps (on the ocean) <note>of Space</note> in the form of <term>Brahmâ</term>—glorified by <term>Sanaka</term> <sup>4</sup> and the Saints (<term>Siddhas</term>)        of <term>Jana-loka</term>, and contemplated by the holy inhabitants of <term>Brahma-loka</term> who are anxious for final liberation—involved in mystic slumber, the celestial personification of his own illusions. This is the dissolution <note>(?) <term>pratisanchara</term></note> termed incidental because <term>Hari</term>        is its incidental <note>Ideal</note> Cause. <sup>5</sup> When the universal spirit wakes, the world revives; when he closes his eyes, all things fall upon the bed of mystic slumber. Just as a thousand great ages constitute a day of <term>Brahmâ</term> <note>in the original, it is <term>Padmayoni</term>, the same as <term>Abjayoni</term>, “Lotus-born,” not <term>Brahmâ</term></note>, so his night consists of the same period.        Waking at the end of his night, the unborn <sup>6</sup>        creates the universe anew.

This is "Incidental" <term>Pralaya</term>; what is the Elemental <note><term>Prâkritika</term></note> Dissolution? <term>Parâshara</term> describes it to <term>Maitreya</term> as follows:

> When, through drought and fire, all the worlds and <term>Pâtâlas</term> <note>Hells</note> are withered up,<sup>1</sup> the progress of elemental dissolution begins. When the universe is thus pervaded by the waves of the watery element, its rudimental flavor is licked up by the element of fire... and the waters themselves are destroyed and become one with fire. The universe is, therefore, entirely filled with <note>ethereal</note> flame, which gradually overspreads the whole world. While space is <note>one</note> flame, the element of wind seizes upon the rudimental property, or form, which is the cause of light; and when that is withdrawn <note><term>pralina</term></note>, everything becomes the nature of air. The rudiment of form being destroyed, and fire <note><term>Vibhâvasu</term>?</note> deprived of its rudiment, air extinguishes fire and spreads over space, which is deprived of light, as fire merges into air. By the loss of this, air is destroyed, and ether <note><term>Kha</term>?</note> remains unmodified. This is the final <term>PRALAYA</term><sup>2</sup>—the Death of the Cosmos; after which its Spirit rests in <term>Nirvâna</term>, or in THAT for which there is neither Day nor Night. All the other <term>Pralayas</term> are periodical and follow the <term>Manvantaras</term> in regular succession, just as the night follows the day of every human creature, animal, and plant. The cycle of creation of the *lives* of the Cosmos is completed, the energy of the manifested “Word” having its growth, peak, and decrease, as do all temporary things, no matter how long their duration. The Creative Force is Eternal as a <term>Noumenon</term>; as a phenomenal manifestation, in its various aspects, it has a *beginning* and must, therefore, have an end. During that interval, it has its periods of activity and its periods of rest. And these are the Days and the Nights of <term>Brahmâ</term>. But <term>Brahman</term>, the <term>Noumenon</term>, never rests, as IT never changes, but ever IS, though IT cannot be said to be anywhere. . . .

The Jewish Kabbalists felt the necessity of this *immutability* in an eternal, infinite Deity, and therefore applied the same thought to the anthropomorphic God. The idea is poetic and very appropriate in its application. In the *Zohar*, we read as follows:

> As Moses was keeping a vigil on Mount Sinai, in company with the Deity, who was concealed from his sight by a cloud, he felt a great fear overcome him, and suddenly asked, “Lord, where are you . . . do you sleep, O Lord?” And the Spirit answered him, “I never sleep; were I to fall asleep for a moment *BEFORE MY TIME*, all of creation would crumble into dissolution in one instant.”

“*Before my time*” is very suggestive. It shows the God of Moses to be only a temporary substitute, like <term>Brahmâ</term>, the male—a substitute and an aspect of THAT which is immutable, and which, therefore, can take no part in the “days” or in the “nights,” nor have any concern whatever with reaction or dissolution.

The latter is the key of the exoteric Churches and is not worth discussion. Rivers see their waves exhausted, the ocean shows its sandy bottom, and plants die. Men and animals decrease in size daily. Life and motion lose their force; planets can hardly gravitate in space; they are extinguished one by one, like a lamp which the hand of the chokra <note>servant</note> neglects to replenish. Sûrya <note>the Sun</note> flickers and goes out, matter falls into dissolution <note>Pralaya</note>, and Brahmâ merges back into Dyaus, the Unrevealed God; and, his task being accomplished, he falls asleep. Another day has passed, night sets in, and continues until the future Dawn.

And now again he re-enters into the golden egg of his Thought—the germs of all that exist—as the divine Man tells us. During His peaceful rest, the animated beings, endowed with the principles of action, cease their functions, and all feeling <note>Manas</note> becomes dormant. When they are all absorbed in the SUPREME SOUL, this Soul of all beings sleeps in complete repose, until the Day when it resumes its form and awakes again from its primitive darkness. <note>¹ See Jacolliot's *The Sons of God* (Les Fils de Dieu), and *India of the Brahmins* (l'Inde des Brahmes), p. 230</note>

As the "*Satya Yuga*" is always the first in the series of the Four Ages or Yugas, so the Kali ever comes last. The Kali Yuga now reigns supreme in India, and it seems to coincide with that of the Western Age. In any case, it is curious to see how prophetic in almost all things the writer of the *Vishnu Purāna* was when foretelling to Maitreya some of the dark influences and sins of this Kali Yuga. For after saying that the "barbarians" will be masters of the banks of the Indus, of Chandrabhâgâ, and Kâshmîra, he adds:

> <note>There</note> will be contemporary monarchs reigning over the earth, kings of a churlish spirit and violent temper, who are constantly addicted to falsehood and wickedness. They will inflict death on women, children, and cows; they will seize the property of their subjects <note>or, according to another reading, be intent upon the wives of others</note>; they will be of limited power . . . their lives will be short, and their desires insatiable.
>
> People of various countries intermingling with them will follow their example; and, the barbarians being powerful <note>in India</note> through the patronage of the princes, while purer tribes are neglected, the people will perish <note>or, as the commentator has it, "the Mlechchhas will be in the center, and the Âryas at the end"</note>. <note>² If this is not prophetic, what is?</note> Wealth and piety will decrease day by day, until the world is wholly depraved.
>
> Property alone will confer rank; wealth will be the only source of devotion; passion will be the sole bond of union between the sexes; falsehood will be the only means of success in litigation; and women will be objects merely of sensual gratification. External appearances will be the only distinction of the several orders of life; dishonesty <note>anyâya</note> will be the universal means of subsistence; weakness will be the cause of dependence; threats and presumption will be substituted for learning; charity will be seen as devotion; mutual consent will constitute marriage; fine clothes will be dignity. He who is the strongest will reign. The people, unable to bear the heavy burdens <note>khara-bhâra, load of taxes</note>, will take refuge among the valleys. Thus, in the Kali age, decay shall constantly proceed, until the human race approaches its annihilation <note>pralaya</note>. When the close of the Kali age is near, a portion of that divine being who exists by his own spiritual nature <note>Kalki Avatâra</note> shall descend upon earth, endowed with the eight superhuman faculties. He will re-establish righteousness upon earth, and the minds of those who live at the end of the Kali age shall be awakened, and shall be as clear as crystal. The men who are thus changed . . . shall be as *the seeds of human beings*, and shall give birth to a race who shall follow the laws of the Krita age.

# SECTION 8

## THE LOTUS AS A UNIVERSAL SYMBOL

There are no ancient symbols without a deep and philosophical meaning attached to them, and their importance and significance increase with their antiquity. Such is the Lotus. It is the flower sacred to Nature and her Gods, and it represents the Abstract and the Concrete Universes, standing as the emblem of the productive powers of both spiritual and physical nature. It was held as sacred from the remotest antiquity by the Aryan Hindus, the Egyptians, and by the Buddhists after them. It was revered in China and Japan, and adopted as a Christian emblem by the Greek and Latin Churches, who made it a messenger—just as Christians do now, having replaced it with the water-lily.

[In the Christian religion, in every picture of the Annunciation, Gabriel the Archangel appears to the Virgin Mary holding a spray of water-lilies in his hand. This spray, typifying Fire and Water, or the idea of creation and generation, symbolizes *precisely the same idea* as *the Lotus* in the hand of the Bodhisattva who announces to Maha-maya, Gautama's mother, the birth of Buddha, the world's Savior. Thus also were Osiris and Horus constantly represented by the Egyptians in association with the Lotus flower, both being Sun-Gods or Fire; just as the Holy Ghost is still typified by "tongues of fire" in the Acts.]

# THE LOTUS, AS A UNIVERSAL SYMBOL

The Maharajas of the STANZAS, representing the four quarters of Heaven, each stand on a Lotus. The Lotus is the twofold symbol of the Divine and Human Hermaphrodite, being, so to speak, of dual sex.

Among the Hindus, the Spirit of Fire (or Heat)—which stirs up, fertilizes, and develops everything born of WATER or Primordial Earth into concrete form from its ideal prototype—evolved Brahma. The Lotus flower is depicted as growing out of the navel of Vishnu, the God who rests on the waters of Space upon the Serpent of Infinity; this is the most graphic symbol¹ ever created. It represents the Universe evolving from the central Sun, the POINT, the ever-concealed Germ. Lakshmi, the female aspect of Vishnu—who is also called *Padma* (the Lotus) in the *Ramayana*—is likewise shown floating on a Lotus flower at the “Creation” and during the “churning of the ocean” of Space. She is also shown springing from the “Sea of Milk,” much like Venus-Aphrodite rose from the foam of the ocean.

> ->Then, seated on a lotus,<-
> ->Beauty’s bright Goddess, peerless Shri, arose<-
> ->Out of the waves<-

writes the English Orientalist and poet, Sir Monier Williams.

The underlying idea in this symbol is very beautiful and, furthermore, demonstrates an identical origin in all religious systems. Whether represented as the Lotus or the water lily, it signifies the same philosophical idea: namely, the emanation of the objective from the subjective—divine Ideation passing from the abstract into concrete or visible form. For as soon as DARKNESS—or rather, what appears as “darkness” to the ignorant—has disappeared into its own realm of Eternal Light, leaving behind only its divine manifested Ideation, the creative Logoi have their understanding opened. They see in the Ideal World (previously hidden within Divine Thought) the archetypal forms of everything, and they proceed to copy, build, or fashion evanescent and transcendent forms based on these models.

At this stage of Action, the Demiurge is not yet the Architect. Born in the Twilight of Action, he must first perceive the Plan and realize the Ideal Forms that lie buried within Eternal Ideation, just as the future lotus leaves and immaculate petals are hidden within the seed of the plant.²

Having evolved himself from the Soul of the World, once separated from the First Cause, he expands and emanates all Nature out of himself. # THE SECRET DOCTRINE

In a chapter of the *Book of the Dead*, called “Transformation into the Lotus,” the God, depicted as a head emerging from this flower, exclaims:

> I am the pure Lotus, emerging from the Luminous Ones . . . I carry the messages of Horus . . . I am the pure Lotus which comes from the Solar Fields.<note>Chapter 81</note>

The lotus idea may be traced even in the Elohistic first chapter of *Genesis*, as stated in *Isis Unveiled*. It is to this idea that we must look for the origin and explanation of the verse in the Jewish Cosmogony which reads: “And God said, Let the earth bring forth . . . the fruit-tree yielding fruit after its kind, whose seed is in itself.”<note>Genesis 1:11</note> In all the primitive religions, the Creative God is the “Son of the Father,” that is to say, his Thought made visible; and before the Christian era, from the Trimûrti of the Hindus down to the three Kabalistic Heads of the Scriptures, as explained by the Jews, the Triune Godhead of each nation was fully defined and substantiated in its allegories.

Such is the cosmic and ideal significance of this great symbol with the Eastern peoples. But when applied to practical and exoteric worship, which also had its esoteric symbology, the Lotus, in time, became the carrier and container of a more earthly idea. No dogmatic religion has ever escaped having a sexual element in it; and to this day it stains the moral beauty of the root idea of symbology. The following is quoted from the same Kabalistic manuscript which we have already cited on several occasions:

> Pointing to a similar meaning was the lotus growing in the waters of the Nile. Its mode of growth peculiarly fitted it as a symbol of the generative activities. The flower of the lotus, which is the bearer of the seed for reproduction as the result of its maturing, is connected with its placenta-like attachments to mother-earth, or the womb of Isis, through the water of the womb—that is, the river Nile—by the long cord-like stalk, the umbilicus. Nothing can be clearer than the symbol, and to make it perfect in its intended meaning, a child is sometimes represented as seated in or issuing from the flower.<note>In the Indian Purânas, it is Vishnu, the First, and Brahma, the Second Logos—or the ideal and practical creators—who are respectively represented: one as manifesting the lotus, the other as issuing from it.</note> Thus Osiris and Isis, the children of Kronos, or time without end, in the development of their nature forces, in this picture become the parents of man under the name Horus.<note>See Section 9, “The Moon, Deus Lunus, Phoebe”</note>

We cannot place too much emphasis upon the use of this generative function as a basis for a symbolic language and a scientific art-speech. Thought upon the idea leads at once to reflection upon the subject of the creative cause. With the Brâhmans, who have never invested the natural procreative functions of mankind with an "original sin" element, it is a religious duty to have a son. A Brâhman, in days of old, having accomplished his mission as a human creator, retired to the jungle and passed the rest of his days in religious meditation. He had accomplished his duty to nature, as a mortal man and its co-worker, and henceforth gave all his thoughts to the spiritual and immortal portion of himself, regarding the terrestrial as a mere illusion, an evanescent dream—which, indeed it is. With the Semite, it was different. He invented a temptation of the flesh in a garden of Eden, and showed his God—esoterically, the Tempter and the Ruler of Nature—CURSING forever an act which was in the logical program of that Nature. <note>The same idea is carried out exoterically in the incidents of the exodus from Egypt. At the same time, esoterically, he regarded the supposed sin and FALL as an act so sacred that he chose the organ, the perpetrator of the *original sin*, as the fittest and most sacred symbol to represent that God, who is shown as branding its entry into function as disobedience and everlasting SIN!

Who can ever fathom the paradoxical depths of the Semitic mind! And this paradoxical element, *without* its innermost significance, has now passed entirely into Christian theology and dogma!

# THE LOTUS, AS A UNIVERSAL SYMBOL

Whether the early Fathers of the Church knew the esoteric meaning of the Hebrew Old *Testament*, or whether only a few of them were aware of it while the others remained ignorant of the secret, is a matter for future generations to decide. One thing, at any rate, is certain. As the Esotericism of the *New Testament* agrees perfectly with that of the Hebrew Mosaic Books, and since, at the same time, a number of purely Egyptian symbols and Pagan dogmas in general—the Trinity, for example—have been copied and incorporated into the *Synoptic Gospels* and *St. John*, it becomes evident that the identity of those symbols was known to the writers of the *New Testament*, whoever they may have been. They must have also been aware of the priority of Egyptian Esotericism, since they adopted several symbols which typify purely Egyptian concepts and beliefs, in both their outward and inward meanings, which are not to be found in the *Jewish Canon*. One of these is the water-lily in the hands of the Archangel in early representations of his appearance to the Virgin Mary; these symbolic images are preserved to this day in the iconography of the Greek and Roman Churches. Thus, Water, Fire, and the Cross, as well as the Dove, the Lamb, and other *Sacred Animals*, with all their combinations, esoterically yield an identical meaning, and must have been accepted as an improvement upon Judaism, pure and simple.

For the Lotus and Water are among the oldest symbols, and in their origin are purely *Âryan*, though they became common property during the branching off of the Fifth Race. To give an example: letters, as well as numbers, were all mystic, whether in combination or taken separately. The most sacred of all is the letter *M*. It is both feminine and masculine, or androgynous, and is made to symbolize WATER in its origin—the great deep. It is a mystic letter in all languages, Eastern and Western, and stands as a glyph for the waves, thus: <image-desc>a glyph representing waves, consisting of three connected zigzag peaks</image-desc>. In *Âryan* Esotericism, as in Semitic, this letter has always stood for the Waters. In Sanskrit, for instance, MAKARA, the tenth sign of the Zodiac, means a crocodile, or rather an aquatic monster always associated with Water. The letter MA is equivalent to and corresponds with the number 5, which is composed of a *Binary* (the symbol of the two sexes separated) and a *Ternary* (the symbol of the Third Life, the offspring of the *Binary*). This, again, is often symbolized by a *Pentagon*, the latter being a sacred sign, a divine Monogram. MAITREYA is the secret name of the *Fifth Buddha*, and the *Kalki Avatâra* of the *Brâhmans*, the last MESSIAH who will come at the culmination of the Great Cycle. It is also the initial letter of the Greek Metis, or *Divine Wisdom*; of Mimra, the "*Word*," or Logos; and of *Mithras* (the Mihr), the *Monad*, *Mystery*.
