Will this be called a coincidence? It is a strange one, indeed, when we see even Moses—found in the water of the Nile—having this symbolic consonant in his name. And Pharaoh’s daughter “called his name Moses, and she said, ‘Because I drew him out of the Water.’”¹ In addition, the Hebrew sacred name of God associated with the letter M is *Meborach*, meaning the “Holy” or the “Blessed,” and the name for the water of the *Flood* is *M'bul*. A reminder of the “three Maries” at the Crucifixion and their connection with *Mare* (the sea or water) may conclude these examples. This is why, in Judaism and Christianity, the Messiah is always connected with water and baptism; and also with the fish—the sign of the Zodiac called *Minam* in Sanskrit—and even with the *Matsya* (Fish) *Avatâra* and the lotus, which is a symbol of the womb, or with the water-lily, which has the same meaning.

Among the relics of ancient Egypt, the older the votive symbols and emblems found, the more frequently lotus flowers and water are seen in connection with the Solar Gods. The God Khnoom—the “Moist Power” or Water, which Thales taught was the principle of all things—sits on a throne enshrined in a lotus. The God Bes stands on a lotus, ready to devour his offspring. Thoth, the God of Mystery and Wisdom and the sacred scribe of Amenti, wearing the solar disk as headgear, sits with a bull’s head—the sacred bull of Mendes being a form of Thoth—and a human body on a full-blown lotus. Finally, it is the Goddess Hiquit, in the form of a frog, who rests on the lotus, thus showing her connection with water. And it is from the unpoetic shape of this frog symbol—undeniably the glyph of the most ancient Egyptian deities—that Egyptologists have been trying in vain to unravel the goddess's mystery and functions. Its adoption in the Church by early Christians shows that they understood it better than our modern Orientalists do. The “frog or toad Goddess” was one of the primary Cosmic Deities connected with creation because of the animal’s amphibious nature and especially because of its apparent resurrection after long ages of

# SECTION 9

## THE MOON; DEUS LUNUS, PHŒBE

This ancient symbol is the most poetic of all symbols, as well as the most philosophical. The ancient Greeks brought it into prominence, and modern poets have used it until it is nearly exhausted. The Queen of Night, riding in the majesty of her peerless light in Heaven, casting everything—even Hesperus—into darkness, and spreading her silver mantle over the whole sidereal world, has always been a favorite theme for all the poets of Christendom, from Milton and Shakespeare down to the latest versifier. But the radiant lamp of night, with her suite of unnumbered stars, spoke only to the imagination of the uninitiated. Until recently, Religion and Science had nothing to do with this beautiful myth. Yet, the cold, chaste Moon—she who, in the words of Shelley:

> . . . . . . . . makes all beautiful on which she smiles
> That wandering shrine of soft yet icy flame
> Which ever is transformed, yet still the same,
> And warms not but illumes . . . . . . . . <sup>1</sup>

stands in closer relation to Earth than any other sidereal orb. The Sun is the giver of Life to the whole Planetary System; the Moon is the Giver of Life to our Globe, and the early races understood and knew it, even in their infancy. She is the Queen, and she is the King. She was King Soma before she was transformed into Phœbe and the chaste Diana. She is pre-eminently the Deity of the Christians, through the Mosaic and Kabalistic Jews, though the civilized world may have remained ignorant of this fact for long ages—in fact, ever since the last initiated Father of the Church died, carrying the secrets of the pagan temples with him into his grave. For such “Fathers” as Origen or Clemens Alexandrinus, the Moon was Jehovah’s living symbol: the giver of Life and the giver of Death, the disposer of Being in our World. For, if Artemis was *Luna* in Heaven, and, to the Greeks, Diana on Earth (who presided over childbirth and life), to the Egyptians she was Hekat (Hecate) in Hell, the Goddess of Death, who ruled over magic and enchantments. More than this; as the personified Moon, whose phenomena are triple, Diana-Hecate-Luna is *the three in one*. For she is *Diva triformis*,

The number seven, so prominent in the *Bible* and so sacred in the seventh day, or Sabbath, came to the Jews from antiquity. It derived its origin from the four groups of seven contained in the 28 days of the lunar month, with each seven-day portion being represented by one quarter of the Moon.

It is worthwhile to present in this work a bird’s-eye view of the origin and development of the lunar myth and worship in historical antiquity on our side of the globe. Its earlier origin cannot be traced by exact Science, which rejects all tradition; meanwhile, for Theology—which, under the guidance of the crafty Popes, has condemned every fragment of literature that does not bear the *imprimatur* of the Church of Rome—its ancient history is a sealed book. Whether Egyptian or Aryan Hindu religious philosophy is older—the SECRET DOCTRINE says it is the latter—does not matter much in this instance, as Lunar and Solar “worship” are the oldest in the world. Both have survived and prevail to this day throughout the whole world: openly for some, and for others—such as in Christian symbolism—secretly. The cat, a lunar symbol, was sacred to Isis, who was the Moon in one sense just as Osiris was the Sun, and it is often seen on top of the *sistrum* in the hand of the Goddess. This animal was held in great veneration in the city of Bubastis, which went into deep mourning upon the death of the sacred cats, because Isis, as the Moon, was worshipped specifically in that city of mysteries. The astronomical symbolism connected with it has already been given in Section 1, and no one has described it better than Mr. Gerald Massey in his *Lectures* and in *The Natural Genesis*. It is said that the eye of the cat seems to follow the lunar phases in their growth and decline, and its eyes shine like two stars in the darkness of night. This leads to the mythological allegory showing Diana hiding in the Moon in the form of a cat when she was seeking, along with other deities, to escape the pursuit of Typhon, as related in Ovid's *Metamorphoses*. In Egypt, the Moon was both the “Eye of Horus” and the “Eye of Osiris” (the Sun).

The same applies to the *Cynocephalus*. The dog-headed ape was a glyph used to symbolize the Sun and Moon in turn, though the *Cynocephalus* is more of a *Hermetic* symbol than a religious one. It is the hieroglyph of the planet Mercury and of the "Mercury" of the alchemical philosophers, who say that:

Mercury must always be near Isis, *as her minister*, for without Mercury, neither Isis nor Osiris can accomplish anything in the GREAT WORK.

Therefore, the meaning of the “fairy tale”—translated by Chwolsohn from the Arabic version of an old Chaldean manuscript about Qû-tâmy being instructed by the *idol* of the Moon—is easily understood. Seldenus tells us the secret, as does Maimonides in his *Guide to the Perplexed*.¹ The worshippers of the <term>Teraphim</term> (the Jewish Oracles) carved images and claimed that as the light of the principal stars [planets] permeated these through and through, the Angelic VIRTUES [or the Regents of the stars and planets] conversed with them, teaching them many most useful things and arts. Those who traced out the στοιχεῖα were called στοιχειωματικοί, or diviners by the στοιχεῖα.²

It is sentences like these in the *Nabathean Agriculture*, however, which have frightened men of science and made them proclaim the work “either an apocryphon or a fairy tale, unworthy of the notice of an Academician.” At the same time, as shown, zealous Roman Catholics and Protestants metaphorically tore it to pieces; the former because “it described the worship of demons,” and the latter because it was “ungodly.” Once more, they are all wrong. Solar and lunar worship, as well as the worship of the stars and elements, can be traced and appear in Christian theology. These are defended by Roman Catholics and can be stoutly denied by Protestants only at their own risk and peril. Two instances may be given.

Ammianus Marcellinus teaches that ancient divinations were always accomplished with the help of the Spirits of the Elements (*Spiritus Elementorum*, and in Greek, πνεύματα τῶν στοιχείων).

## DEMON EST DEUS INVERSUS

THIS symbolic sentence, in its many-sided forms, is certainly most dangerous and iconoclastic when facing all the later dualistic religions—or rather, theologies—and especially so in the light of Christianity. Yet it is neither fair nor correct to say that it is Christianity that conceived and brought forth Satan. As an "adversary"—the opposing Power required for the equilibrium and harmony of things in Nature, just as Shadow is required to make the Light even brighter, as Night brings the Day into greater relief, and as Cold makes one appreciate the comfort of Heat all the more—so has SATAN always existed. Homogeneity is one and indivisible. But if the homogeneous One and Absolute is no mere figure of speech, and if Heterogeneity, in its dualistic aspect, is its offspring—its two-forked shadow or reflection—then even that divine Homogeneity must contain within itself the essence of both good and evil. If "God" is Absolute, Infinite, and the Universal Root of everything in Nature and its Universe, where does Evil (or the D'Evil) come from if not from the same "Golden Womb" of the Absolute? Thus we are forced either to accept the emanation of good and evil, of <term>Agathodæmon</term> and <term>Kakodæmon</term>, as offshoots from the same trunk of the Tree of Being, or to resign ourselves to the absurdity of believing in two eternal Absolutes!

In tracing the origin of the idea back to the very beginnings of the human mind, it is only fair, meanwhile, to give even the proverbial Devil his due. Antiquity knew of no isolated, thoroughly and absolutely bad "god of evil." Pagan thought represented good and evil as twin brothers, born from the same mother—Nature; as soon as that thought ceased to be archaic, Wisdom transformed into Philosophy. In the beginning, the symbols of good and evil were mere abstractions, Light and Darkness; later, their types were chosen from among the most natural and recurring periodic cosmic phenomena—the Day and Night, or the Sun and Moon. Then the hosts of the Solar and Lunar Deities were made to represent them, and the Dragon of Darkness was contrasted with the Dragon of Light. The HOST of Satan is a Son of God, no

# DEMON EST DEUS INVERSUS

The student will do well to remember that, among every people except the Christian nations, the Devil is to this day no worse an entity than the opposite aspect in the dual nature of the so-called Creator. This is only natural. One cannot claim God as the synthesis of the whole universe—as omnipresent, omniscient, and infinite—and then divorce him from evil. Since there is far more evil than good in the world, it follows on logical grounds that either God must include evil, stand as the direct cause of it, or else surrender his claims to absoluteness. The ancients understood this so well that their philosophers, followed now by the Kabalists, defined evil as the “lining” of God or good; *Demon est Deus inversus* <note>The Devil is God inverted</note> is a very old adage. Indeed, evil is but an antagonizing blind force in Nature; it is reaction, opposition, and contrast—evil for some, good for others. There is no *malum in se* <note>absolute evil</note>; there is only the shadow of light, without which light could have no existence, even in our perceptions. If evil disappeared, good would disappear along with it from Earth. The “Old Dragon” was pure Spirit before he became Matter, *passive* before he became *active*. In Syro-Chaldean Magic, both Ophis and Ophiomorphos are joined in the Zodiac in the sign of the androgyne *Virgo-Scorpio*. Before its fall on earth, the “Serpent” was *Ophis-Christos*, and after its fall it became Ophiomorphos-CHRESTOS. Everywhere the speculations of the Kabalists treat evil as a FORCE which is antagonistic but, at the same time, essential to good, as it gives it the vitality and existence it could never have otherwise. There would be no *life* possible (in the mâyâvic sense) without *death*, and no regeneration or reconstruction without destruction. Plants would perish in eternal sunlight, as would man, who would become an automaton without the exercise of his free will and his aspiring toward that sunlight, which would lose its being and value for him if he had nothing but light. Good is infinite and eternal only in what is eternally concealed from us, and this is why we imagine it to be eternal. On the manifested planes, one balances the other. There are few theists—believers in a personal God—who do not make Satan the shadow of God, or who, confusing both, do not believe they have a right to pray to their idol, asking its help and protection for the exercise of and immunity for their evil and cruel deeds. “Lead us not into temptation” is addressed daily to “our Father in Heaven,” and not to the Devil, by millions of Christian hearts. # SECTION 12

## THE THEOGONY OF THE CREATIVE GODS

To thoroughly understand the idea underlying every ancient cosmology requires the study and comparative analysis of all the great religions of antiquity, for it is only by this method that the root idea can be made plain. Exact science, if it could soar so high in tracing the operations of nature to their ultimate and original sources, would call this idea the hierarchy of forces. The original transcendental and philosophical conception was one. But as systems began to reflect the idiosyncrasies of nations more and more with every age—and as the latter, after separating, settled into distinct groups, each evolving along its own national or tribal groove—the main idea gradually became veiled by the overgrowth of human fancy. While in some countries the FORCES, or rather the intelligent powers of nature, received divine honors to which they were hardly entitled, in others—as now in Europe and the other civilized lands—the very thought of such forces being endowed with intelligence seems absurd and is proclaimed *unscientific*. Therefore, one finds relief in statements such as those found in the introduction to *Asgard and the Gods: Tales and Traditions of our Northern Ancestors*, edited by W.S.W. Anson, who says:

> “Although in Central Asia, on the banks of the Indus, in the Land of the Pyramids, in the Greek and Italian peninsulas, and even in the North, where Celts, Teutons, and Slavs wandered, the religious conceptions of the people have taken different forms, yet their common origin is still perceptible. We point out this connection between the stories of the gods, the deep thought contained in them, and their importance, in order that the reader may see that it is not a magic world of erratic fancy which is opened before him, but that life and nature formed the basis for the existence and action of these divinities.” <note>Page 3</note>

And though it is impossible for any occultist or student of Eastern esotericism to agree with the strange idea that “the religious conceptions of the most famous nations of antiquity are connected with the beginnings of civilization among the Germanic races,” <note>Ibid., page 2</note> he is nonetheless glad to find such truths.

## THE THEOGONY OF THE CREATIVE GODS

expressed as that. “These fairy tales are not senseless stories written for the amusement of the idle; they embody the profound religion of our ancestors.” ¹

Precisely so. Not only their religion, but likewise their history. For a myth, in Greek *mythos* (μῦθος), means oral tradition, passed from mouth to mouth from one generation to the next; and even in modern etymology, the term stands for a mythical statement conveying some important truth. It is a tale of some extraordinary personage whose biography has become overgrown with rich popular fancy—owing to the veneration of successive generations—but which is no total fable. Like our ancestors, the primitive Aryans, we believe firmly in the personality and intelligence of more than one phenomenon-producing force in nature.

As time rolled on, the archaic teaching grew dimmer, and the nations more or less lost sight of the highest and single Principle of all things. They began to transfer the abstract attributes of the “causeless cause” to the caused effects, which became in their turn causative: the creative powers of the universe. The great nations acted in this way from fear of profaning the IDEA; the smaller nations did so because they either failed to grasp it or lacked the power of philosophical conception needed to preserve it in all its immaculate purity. But one and all, with the exception of the latest Aryans—who have now become Europeans and Christians—show this veneration in their cosmogonies. As Thomas Taylor,² the most intuitive of all the translators of the Greek fragments, shows, no nation has ever conceived the One Principle as the immediate creator of the visible universe; for no sane man would credit a planner and architect with having built the edifice he admires with his own hands. On the testimony of Damascius in his work, *On First Principles* (Περὶ Πρώτων Ἀρχῶν), they referred to it as the “Unknown <term>DARKNESS</term>.” The Babylonians passed over this principle in silence. “To that god,” says Porphyry in his *On Abstinence* (Περὶ ἀποχῆς τῶν ἐμψύχων)³, “who is above all things, neither external speech ought to be addressed, nor yet that which is inward.” Hesiod begins his *Theogony* with the words, “Chaos of all things was the first produced,” ⁴ thus allowing the inference that its cause or producer must be passed over in reverential silence. Homer in his poems ascends no higher than <term>Night</term>, whom he represents Zeus as reverencing. In the Norse Cosmogony, it is again the same.

In the beginning, there was a great abyss [Chaos]; neither day nor night existed. The abyss was <term>Ginnungagap</term>, the yawning gulf, without beginning and without end. All-Father, the Uncreated and the Unseen, dwelled in the depth of the abyss [Space] and willed, and what He willed came into being. <note>1. *Asgard and the Gods*, p. 22</note>

As in the Hindu Cosmogony, the evolution of the Universe is divided into two acts, which are called in India the *<term>Prâkrita</term>* and *<term>Padma</term>* Creations. Before the warm rays pouring from the “Home of Brightness” awaken life in the Great Waters of Space, the Elements of the First Creation come into view. From them is formed the Giant <term>Ymir</term>, or <term>Oergelmir</term> (literally, *seething clay*), primordial matter differentiated from Chaos. Then comes the cow <term>Audumla</term>, the Nourisher, <note>2. <term>Vâch</term>—the “melodious cow, who milks sustenance and Water,” and yields us “nourishment and sustenance,” as described in the *<term>Rig Veda</term>*.</note> from whom is born <term>Buri</term> (the Producer), whose son <term>Bor</term> (Born), by <term>Bestla</term>, the daughter of the “Frost-Giants” (the sons of <term>Ymir</term>), had three sons: <term>Odin</term>, <term>Willi</term>, and <term>We</term>, or “Spirit,” “Will,” and “Holiness.” <note>3. Compare *The Genesis of the Primordial Races*, in this work.</note> This was when Darkness still reigned throughout Space, when the <term>Ases</term>, the creative Powers, or <term>Dhyân Chohans</term>, were not yet evolved, and the <term>Yggdrasil</term>, the tree of the Universe of Time and of Life, had not yet grown, and there was, as yet, no <term>Walhalla</term>, or Hall of Heroes. 

The Scandinavian legends of Creation, regarding our Earth and World, begin with *Time* and human Life. All that precedes it is, for them, “Darkness,” in which All-Father, the Cause of all, dwells. As observed by the editor of *Asgard and the Gods*, though these legends contain the idea of that ALL-FATHER as the original cause of all, “he is scarcely more than mentioned in the poems.” This is not, as the editor thinks, because the idea “could not develop into clear concepts of the Eternal” before the preaching of the Gospel, but rather because of its deep esoteric character. Therefore, all the creative Gods, or *personal* Deities, begin at the secondary stage of Cosmic Evolution. <term>Zeus</term> is born *in*, and out of <term>Kronos</term>—Time. So is <term>Brahmâ</term> the production and emanation of *<term>Kâla</term>*, “eternity and time,” *<term>Kâla</term>* being one of the names of <term>Vishnu</term>. Consequently, we find <term>Odin</term> is the Father *of the Gods and of the Ases*, just as <term>Brahmâ</term> is...

Space exists only as *visible* light and heat, with the Sun being merely the agent of these forces. This is the first triadic <term>hypostasis</term>. The quaternary is composed of the energizing *light* shed by the <term>Logos</term>.

The Hebrew <term>Kabbalists</term> expressed this in a manner that is esoterically identical to the <term>Vedantic</term> view. They taught that <term>Ain Soph</term> could not be comprehended, located, or named, even though it is the Causeless Cause of all. Therefore, its name, <term>Ain Soph</term>, is a term of negation: "the inscrutable, the unrecognizable, and the unnameable." Consequently, they represented it as a Boundless Circle—a Sphere of which the human intellect, even at its furthest stretch, could only perceive the outer vault. In the words of one who has most thoroughly unriddled much of the <term>Kabbalistic</term> system—in one of its meanings, specifically its numerical and geometrical esotericism:

> Close your eyes, and from your own consciousness of perception, try to think outward to the furthest limits in every direction. You will find that equal lines or rays of perception extend out evenly in all directions, so that the greatest effort of perception will end in the *vault of a sphere*. The limit of this sphere will, of course, be a great *circle*, and the direct rays of thought in any and every direction must be *straight line radii of the circle*. This, then, *must* be, humanly speaking, the furthest all-embracing conception of the <term>Ain Soph</term> *manifested*, which expresses itself as a *geometrical figure*—namely, a circle with its elements of a curved circumference and a straight line diameter divided into radii. Consequently, a geometrical shape is the first recognizable means of connection between the <term>Ain Soph</term> and human intelligence. <note>*The Masonic Review*, June 1886</note>

This Great Circle—which Eastern Esotericism reduces to the Point within the Boundless Circle—is the <term>Avalokiteshvara</term>, the <term>Logos</term>, or *<term>Verbum</term>*, of which <term>T. Subba Row</term> speaks. But this Circle, or *manifested* God, is as unknown to us (except through its *manifested* Universe) as the *ONE* is, though it is easier—or rather, more possible—for our highest concepts to grasp. This <term>Logos</term> sleeps in the heart of <term>Parabrahman</term> during <term>Pralaya</term>, just as our "Ego is latent [in us] at the time of *<term>sushupti</term>*" (or deep sleep). It cannot perceive <term>Parabrahman</term> except as *<term>Mulaprakriti</term>*—the latter being a Cosmic Veil which is "the mighty expanse of cosmic matter." Thus, the <term>Logos</term> is only an organ in cosmic Creation through which the Energy and Wisdom of <term>Parabrahman</term> radiate—yet this source remains *unknown to the <term>Logos</term>, just as it is unknown to us.* Furthermore, since the <term>Logos</term> is as unknown to us as <term>Parabrahman</term> is actually unknown to the <term>Logos</term>, both Eastern Esotericism and the <term>Kabbalah</term> have broken down this abstract synthesis into concrete images to bring the <term>Logos</term> within reach of our understanding. But there are two distinct aspects in universal Esotericism, both Eastern and Western, in all these personifications of the *female* Power in Nature, or Nature as the *noumenal* and the *phenomenal*. One is its purely metaphysical aspect, as described by the learned lecturer in his "Notes on the <term>Bhagavad Gîtâ</term>"; the other is terrestrial and physical, and at the same time *divine* from the standpoint of practical human understanding and Occultism. And here we may incidentally point out one of the many unjust slurs thrown by "good and pious" missionaries in India upon the religion of that land. The allegory in the <term>Shatapatha Brâhmana</term>—which says that <term>Brahmâ</term>, as the Father of men, performed the work of procreation through incestuous intercourse with his own daughter <term>Vâch</term>, also called <term>Sandhyâ</term> (Twilight) and <term>Shatarûpâ</term> (hundred-formed)—is incessantly thrown in the faces of the Brahmins as a reason to condemn their "detestable, false religion." Europeans conveniently forget the fact that the Patriarch Lot is shown guilty of the same crime in *human form*, whereas <term>Brahmâ</term> (or rather <term>Prajâpati</term>) accomplished the incest in the form of a buck with his daughter, who had taken the form of a hind (*rohit*). Furthermore, the esoteric reading of the third chapter of <term>Genesis</term> shows the same thing. Moreover, there is certainly a *cosmic* rather than a physiological meaning attached to the Indian allegory. As already stated, Aditi-Vâch is the female *Logos*, or *Verbum*—the "Word"—and <term>Sephira</term> in the *Kabalah* is the same. These feminine Logoi are all correlations, in their noumenal aspect, of Light, Sound, and Ether. This demonstrates how well-informed the ancients were in both physical science, as it is known to modern people today, and in the origins of that science within the spiritual and astral spheres.

Our ancient writers said that *Vâch* consists of four kinds. These are called *Parâ, Pashyanti, Madhyamâ,* and *Vaikhari*. You will find this statement in the Rig Veda itself and in several of the Upanishads. *Vaikhari Vâch* is what we utter.

It is sound and *speech*—that which becomes comprehensible and objective to one of our physical senses and can be brought under the laws of perception. Hence:

> Every kind of *vaikhari Vâch* exists in its *madhyamâ*... *pashyantî*, and ultimately in its *parâ* form. The reason why this <term>Pranava</term> <note>1</note> is called *Vâch* is that these four principles of the great Kosmos correspond to these four forms of Vâch. The whole Kosmos in its objective form is *vaikhari Vâch*; the light of the Logos is the *madhyamâ* form; the Logos itself is the *pashyanti* form; and <term>Parabrahman</term> <note>is</note> the *parâ* <note>the aspect beyond the Noumenon of all Noumena</note> of that *Vâch*. <note>2</note>

Thus, Vâch, <term>Shekinah</term>, or the "music of the spheres" of <term>Pythagoras</term> are one and the same, if we take as our examples instances from the three most (apparently) dissimilar religious philosophies in the world: the Hindu, the Greek, and the Chaldean Hebrew. These personifications and allegories may be viewed under *four* (chief) and *three* (lesser) aspects, or *seven* in all, as is customary in Esotericism. The *parâ* form is the ever-subjective and latent Light and Sound which exist eternally in the heart of the INCOGNIZABLE; when transferred into the ideation of the Logos, or its latent *Light*, it is called *pashyantî*; and when it becomes that Light expressed, it is *madhyamâ*.

Now the *Kabalah* provides this definition:

> There are three kinds of light, and a fourth that interpenetrates the others: (1) the clear and penetrating *objective light*, (2) the *reflected light*, and (3) the *abstract light*.

The ten <term>Sephiroth</term>—the *Three* and the *Seven*—are called in the *Kabalah* the "Ten Words" (DBRIM or *Debarim*), the Numbers, and the Emanations of the Heavenly Light, which is both <term>Adam Kadmon</term> and Sephira, <term>Prajâpati-Vâch</term>, or <term>Brahmâ</term>. You exist, but the understanding and vision of mortals cannot reach your existence, nor determine for you the Where, the How, and the Why. You exist, and your existence is so profound and secret that none can penetrate and discover your secrecy. You are Living, but within no time that can be fixed or known; You are Living, but not by a spirit or a soul, for *You are Yourself, the Soul of all Souls*." There is a distance between this Kabbalistic Deity and the biblical Jehovah—the spiteful and revengeful God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who tempted the first and wrestled with the last. No Vedantin would do anything but reject such a Parabrahman!</note> Everywhere there is either a LOGOS—a “LIGHT shining in DARKNESS,” truly—or the Architect of the Worlds is *esoterically* in the plural number. At the end of the first stage of Evolution, they are transformed into the seven stellar Rishis, the Saptarishis, while their *human* doubles appear as Heroes, Kings, and Sages on this earth.

The Esoteric Doctrine of the East has thus provided and struck the keynote—which, under its allegorical disguise, is as scientific as it is philosophical and poetical—and every nation has followed its lead. It is from the exoteric religions that we must dig out the root-idea before we turn to esoteric truths, lest the latter be rejected. # THE THEOGONY OF THE CREATIVE GODS

In the beginning, those symbols were all identical. Take, for instance, the opening sentences in various Cosmogonies; in every case, it is a *circle*, an egg, or a *head*. DARKNESS is always associated with this first symbol and surrounds it, as is shown in the Hindu, the Egyptian, the Chaldeo-Hebrew, and even the Scandinavian systems. Thus, we find black ravens, black doves, black waters, and even black flames; the *seventh tongue* of Agni, the fire-god, being called Kâlî, the “Black,” since it was a black flickering flame. Two *black doves* flew from Egypt and, settling on the oaks of Dodona, gave their names to the Greek Gods. Noah sends out a *black raven* after the Deluge, which is a symbol for the Cosmic Pralaya, after which began the real creation or evolution of our Earth and Humanity. Odin's “black” ravens fluttered around the Goddess Saga and “whispered to her of the past and of the future.” Now, what is the inner meaning of all those black birds? It is that they are all connected with the primeval Wisdom, which flows out of the pre-cosmic Source of All, symbolized by the Head, the Circle, or the Egg; they all have an identical meaning and relate to the primordial Archetypal Man, Adam Kadmon, the creative origin of all things, which is composed of the Host of Cosmic Powers—the Creative Dhyân Chohans, beyond which all is Darkness.

Let us inquire about the wisdom of the Kabbalah, even veiled and distorted as it now is, to explain in its numerical language an approximate meaning, at least, of the word “raven.” This is its numerical value as given in the *Source of Measures*:

The term *raven* is used but once, and taken as Eth-h' orebv את-הערב = 678, or 113 x 6, while the *Dove* is mentioned five times. Its value is 71, and 71 x 5 || 355. Six diameters, or the Raven, crossing, would divide the circumference of a circle of 355 into 12 parts or compartments, and 355 subdivided for each unit by 6, would equal 213.0, or the *head* <note>beginning</note> in the first verse of *Genesis*. This divided, or subdivided, in the same way, by 2—or the 355 by 12—would give 213 x 2, or the word B'râsh, ב-ראש, or the first word of *Genesis*, with its prepositional prefix, signifying the same concreted general form, astronomically, with the one here intended.$^1$

Now, the secret reading of the first verse in *Genesis* is: “In Râsh (B'râsh)$^2$ or Head, created Gods, the Heavens and the Earth”—it is easy to understand the esoteric meaning of the *Raven*, once the similar meaning of the Flood, or Noah's Deluge, is established. Whatever the many other meanings of this emblematic allegory may be, its *chief* meaning is that of a new Cycle and a new Round—our *Fourth Round*.$^3$ The “Raven,” or the

Numerically, in the Kabbalah, Jehovah, Adam, and Noah are one. And here lies the abyss between the Aryan and Semitic systems, though both are built on the same foundation. As shown by an expounder of the Kabbalah:

> The basic idea underlying the religious philosophy of the Hebrews was that God contained all things within himself and that man was his *image*—man, including woman <note>as androgynes</note>—and that geometry (and the numbers and measures applicable to astronomy) is contained in the terms *man* and *woman*. The apparent incongruity of such a method was eliminated by showing the connection of man and woman with a particular system of numbers, measures, and geometry through the birth-giving time periods, which furnished the connecting link between the terms used and the facts shown, and perfected the method used.

It is argued that, since the primal cause is absolutely unknowable, "the symbol of its first comprehensible *manifestation* was the concept of a circle with its diameter line, so as to simultaneously convey the idea of geometry, phallicism, and astronomy"; this was finally applied to the "significance of simply human generative organs." Hence, the whole cycle of events from Adam and the Patriarchs down to Noah is made to apply to phallic and astronomical uses, with one regulating the other—such as the lunar periods, for instance. Therefore, too, their genesis begins after their departure from the Ark and the end of the Flood—that is, at the Fourth Race. With the Aryan people, it is different.

## THE SEVEN CREATIONS

THERE was neither day nor night, nor sky nor earth, nor darkness nor light, nor any other thing, except only for One, beyond the grasp of the intellect, or That which is <term>Brahma</term>, <term>Pums</term> (spirit), and <term>Pradhâna</term> (<note>crude</note> matter).

Or literally "One Prâdhânika Brahman Spirit THAT was." The "Prâdhânika Brahma Spirit" is <term>Mûlaprakriti</term> and <term>Parabrahman</term>. $^1$

In the <term>Vishnu Purâna</term>, <term>Parâshara</term> says to <term>Maitreya</term>, his pupil:

> I have thus explained to you, excellent <term>Muni</term>, six creations; the creation of the <term>Arvâksrotas</term> beings was the seventh, and was the creation of man. $^2$

<term>Origen</term>, commenting upon the books written by <term>Celsus</term>, his <note>Gnostic</note> opponent—books which were all destroyed by the cautious Church Fathers—evidently answers the objections of his critic and reveals his system at the same time. But the theogony <note>of Celsus</note>, the genesis of the stars or planets, and of sound and color, were met with only satire, and nothing more. <term>Celsus</term>, you see, "desiring to show off his learning," speaks of a ladder of creation with *seven gates*, and on the top of it the eighth, which is ever closed. The mysteries of the Persian <term>Mithras</term> are explained and "musical reasons, moreover, are added." And to these again he strives "to add a second explanation also connected with musical considerations," $^3$ that is to say, with the seven notes of the scale, the seven Spirits of the Stars, and so on.

<term>Valentinus</term> speaks at length about the power of the great Seven, who were summoned to bring forth this universe after <term>Ar(r)hetos</term>, or the Ineffable, whose name is composed of seven letters, had represented the first <term>hebdomad</term>. The *Seven Creations* are found in almost every <term>Purâna</term>. They are all preceded by what Wilson translates as the "undifferentiated Principle," absolute Spirit, independent of any relation with objects of sense.

They are: (1) <term>Mahat-tattva</term>, the Universal Soul, Infinite Intellect, or Divine Mind; (2) [<term>Tanmâtras</term>], <term>Bhûta</term> or *Bhûtasarga*, elemental creation, the first differentiation of Universal undifferentiated Substance; (3) <term>Indriya</term> or <term>Aindriyaka</term>, organic evolution. "These three were the Prâkrita creations, the *developments of undifferentiated nature*, preceded by the undifferentiated principle"; (4) <term>Mukhya</term>, "the fundamental creation (of perceptible things) was that of inanimate bodies"; <note>"And the fourth creation is *here* the primary, for *immovable things* are emphatically known as primary"—according to a commentary translated by Fitzedward Hall in his editing of Wilson's translation</note> (5) <term>Tairyagyonya</term> or <term>Tiryaksrotas</term>, was that of animals; (6) <term>Ûrdhvasrotas</term>, or that of divinities (?) <note>How can "divinities" have been created after the animals? The esoteric meaning of the expression "animals" refers to the germs of all animal life, including man. Man is called a *sacrificial animal*, that is, the only one among the animal creation who sacrifices to the Gods. Moreover, by "sacred animals," the twelve Signs of the Zodiac are often meant in the sacred texts, as already stated.</note>; (7) <term>Arvâksrotas</term>, was that of man. <note>*Vishnu Purâna*, Wilson, *ibid*, pp. 74-75.</note>

This is the order given in the exoteric texts. According to esoteric teaching, there are seven Primary and seven Secondary "Creations"; the former being the Forces *self-evolving* from the one causeless FORCE; the latter showing the manifested Universe emanating from the already differentiated divine Elements.

Esoterically, as well as exoterically, all the above-enumerated Creations stand for the seven periods of Evolution, whether after an "Age" or a "Day" of <term>Brahmâ</term>. This is the teaching *par excellence* of <term>Occult Philosophy</term>, which, however, never uses the term "creation," nor even that of evolution, with regard to *primary* "Creation"; instead, it calls all such Forces the "aspects of the Causeless Force." In the *Bible*, the seven periods are reduced to the six days of creation and the seventh day of rest, and Westerners adhere to the literal meaning. In Hindu Philosophy, when the active Creator has produced the world of Gods, the Germs of all the undifferentiated Elements, and the rudiments of future senses (the world of noumena, in short), the Universe remains unaltered for a "Day of <term>Brahmâ</term>," a period of 4,320,000,000 years. This is the seventh passive Period, or the "Sabbath day" of Eastern Philosophy, following six periods of active evolution. In the <term>Shatapatha Brâhmana</term>, <term>Brahmâ</term> (neuter), the absolute Cause of all Causes, radiates the Gods. Having

<term>Ildabaoth</term> is a copy of <term>Manu</term>, who boasts:

Marcus, whose philosophy was certainly more <term>Pythagorean</term> than anything else, speaks of a revelation to him of the seven Heavens, each sounding one vowel as they pronounced the seven names of the seven (*Angelic*) <term>Hierarchies</term>.

When Spirit has permeated every minute atom of the seven Principles of the <term>Kosmos</term>, then the Secondary Creation begins, following the previously mentioned period of rest.

The mystic meaning of this is that the twelve great transformations of Spirit into matter—the 12,000 Divine Years—take place during the four great Ages, or the first Mahâyuga. Beginning with the metaphysical and the supra-human, it ends in the physical and purely human natures of the Cosmos and Man. Eastern Philosophy can give the number of mortal years that run along the line of spiritual and physical evolutions of the seen and the unseen, even if Western Science fails to do so.

*Primary Creation* is called the *Creation of Light* (Spirit), and the Secondary is called that of Darkness (Matter).² Both are found in *Genesis*.³ The first is the emanation of self-born Gods (Elohim); the second is the emanation of physical Nature.

This is why it is said in the *Zohar*:

> O companions, companions, man as an emanation was both man and woman, as much on the side of the Father as on the side of the Mother. And this is the sense of the words “And Elohim spoke ‘Let there be Light and there was Light’” . . . . And this is the “two-fold Man.” ¹

Light, however, on our plane, is Darkness in the higher spheres.

“Man and woman . . . on the side of the FATHER” (Spirit) refers to the Primary Creation, and on the side of the *Mother* (Matter) refers to the Secondary. The two-fold Man is Adam Kadmon, the male and female abstract prototype and the differentiated Elohim. Man proceeds from the Dhyân Chohan and is a “Fallen Angel,” a God in exile, as will be shown.

# THE SECRET DOCTRINE

THAT, then, precedes manifestation. "The first was Mahat," says the *Linga Purâna*; for the ONE (the THAT) is neither *first* nor *last*, but ALL. Exoterically, however, this manifestation is the work of the "Supreme One"—or rather, a natural effect of an Eternal Cause. As the Commentator says, it might have been understood to mean that Brahmâ was then *created* (?), being identified with Mahat, active intelligence, or the operating will of the Supreme. Esoteric Philosophy interprets it as the "operating LAW."

We believe that the "apple of discord" between the three *Vedântin* Sects—the Advaita, Dvaita, and the Vishishthadvaita—depends on the correct understanding of this tenet in the *Brâhmanas* and *Purânas*. The first argues rightly that Parabrahman—as the absolute ALL, having no relation to the manifested world, and the Infinite having no connection with the Finite—can neither *will* nor *create*. It argues that before Brahmâ, Mahat, Îshvara, or whatever name the Creative Power may be known by, the Creative Gods and everything else are simply an illusory aspect of Parabrahman in the conception of those who conceive them. Meanwhile, the other sects identify the impersonal Cause with the Creator, or Îshvara.

However, for the Vaishnavas, *Mahat* or *Mahâ-Buddhi* is Divine Mind in active operation, or, as Anaxagoras puts it, "an ordering and disposing Mind, which was the cause of all things"—Νοῦς ὁ διακοσμῶν τε καὶ πάντων αἴτιος.

Wilson immediately recognized the suggestive connection between *Mahat* and the Phoenician *Môt*, or *Mut* (who was female to the Egyptians, the Goddess Moot, the Mother). He says that, "like Mahat, she was the first product of the mixture (?) of Spirit and Matter, and the first rudiment of Creation." Brücker² gives it a still more materialistic and anthropomorphic color, stating: "Through its connection, the Spirit produced Môt . . . Hence . . . the seed of every creature and the creation of all things."¹

Nevertheless, the esoteric meaning of the doctrine is visible through every exoteric sentence on the very surface of the old Sanskrit texts that treat of primordial Creation.

The Supreme Soul, the *all-permeating* (Sarvaga) Substance of the World, having entered <note>been drawn</note> into Matter <note>Prakriti</note> and Spirit <note>Purusha</note>, stirred the *mutable and the immutable principles*, once the season of Creation <note>Manvantara</note> had arrived.

### THE SEVEN CREATIONS

In the Phœnician Cosmogony as well, “Spirit mixing with its own principles gives rise to creation”;<note>Brucker, *ibid*.</note> the Orphic Triad shows an identical doctrine, for there *Phanes*, or Eros; Chaos, containing crude *undifferentiated* Cosmic Matter; and Kronos, Time, are the three cooperating principles emanating from the Concealed and Unknowable *Point* which produce the work of “Creation.” And they are the Hindu *Purusha* (Phanes), *Pradhâna* (Chaos), and *Kâla* (Kronos) or *time*. The good Professor Wilson does not like the idea, as no Christian clergyman, however liberal, would. He remarks that “*the mixture* [of the Supreme Spirit or Soul with its own principles] *is not mechanical*, it is *an influence or effect exerted upon intermediate agents which produce effects*.” The sentence in the *Vishnu Purâna*, “as fragrance affects the mind from its proximity merely, and not from any immediate operation upon the mind itself, so the Supreme influenced the elements of creation,” the reverend and erudite Sanskrit scholar correctly explains as: “as perfumes do not delight the mind by actual contact, but by the impression they make upon the sense of smell, which communicates it to the mind”; adding, “the entrance of the Supreme . . . into Spirit, as well as Matter, is *less intelligible* than the view elsewhere taken of it, as the *infusion* of Spirit, identified with the Supreme, into Prakriti or Matter alone.” He prefers the verse in the *Padma Purâna*: “He who is called the *male* (spirit) of Prakriti . . . that same divine Vishnu entered into Prakriti.” This “view” is certainly more akin to the plastic character of certain verses in the *Bible* concerning the Patriarchs, such as Lot and even Adam,<note>Compare *Genesis*, xix, 34-8 and iv, 1.</note> and others of a still more anthropomorphic nature. But it is just that which led Humanity to *Phallicism*, the Christian religion being honeycombed with it, from the first chapter of *Genesis* down to the *Revelation*.

The Esoteric Doctrine teaches that the Dhyân Chohans are the collective aggregate of divine Intelligence or primordial *Mind*, and that the first Manus, the seven “mind-born” Spiritual Intelligences, are identical with them. Hence the Kwan-Shi-Yin, the “*Golden Dragon in whom are the Seven*,” of STANZA 3, is the Primordial Logos, or Brahmâ, the first manifested Creative Power, and the Dhyânic Energies are the Manus, or *Manu-Svâyambhuva* collectively. The direct connection, moreover, between the Manus and Mahat is easy to see. *Manu* is from the root *Man*, to think, and thinking proceeds from the mind. It is, in Cosmogony, the pre-nebular Period.

Thus, as the differentiation of the primordial germ of life must precede the evolution of the Dhyân Chohan of the *Third Group* or Hierarchy of Being in Primary *Creation*, before those Gods can become (*rûpa*) embodied in their first ethereal form, so *animal* creation must for the same reason precede “divine man” on Earth. And this is why we find in the *Purânas* that “the fifth, the Tairyagyonya Creation, was that of animals.”

# SECTION 14

## THE FOUR ELEMENTS

METAPHYSICALLY and esoterically, there is but ONE ELEMENT in Nature, and at its root is the Deity. The so-called seven Elements—of which *five* have already manifested and asserted their existence—are the garment, *the veil of that Deity*. From the essence of this Deity comes MAN, whether considered physically, psychically, mentally, or spiritually. Only four Elements are generally spoken of in later antiquity, while only five are admitted in philosophy. This is because the body of Ether is not fully manifested yet, and its <term>noumenon</term> is still the “Omnipotent Father Æther,” the synthesis of the rest. But what are these “ELEMENTS,” whose compound bodies have now been discovered by Chemistry and Physics to contain countless sub-elements, even the sixty or seventy of which no longer encompass the whole number suspected? <note>See *Addenda*, Sections 11 and 12</note> In any case, let us follow their evolution from their *historical* beginnings.

The Four Elements were fully characterized by Plato when he said that they were that “*which composes* and *decomposes the compound bodies*.” Therefore, <term>Cosmolatry</term> was never, even in its worst aspect, the fetishism that adores or worships the passive external form and matter of any object; instead, it always looked to the *noumenon* within. Fire, Air, Water, and Earth were but the visible clothing—the symbols of the animating, invisible Souls or Spirits, the Cosmic Gods. Worship was offered to them by the ignorant, while the wiser offered simple but respectful recognition. In turn, the *phenomenal* subdivisions of the <term>noumenal</term> Elements were animated by the so-called <term>Elementals</term>, the “Nature Spirits” of lower grades.

In the *Theogony* of <term>Môchus</term>, we find Ether first, and then the Air; these are the two principles from which <term>Ulom</term>, the *intelligible* (νοητὸς) God—the visible Universe of Matter—is born. <note>Movers, *Phœnizer*, p 282</note>

The <term>Astral Light</term> of the Theurgists and Kabbalists is its last and lowest division.

The Elements (στοιχεια) of Plato and Aristotle were thus the *incorporeal principles* attached to the four great divisions of our Cosmic World, and it is with justice that Creuzer defines these primitive beliefs as “*a species of magism, a psychic paganism, and a deification of potencies; a spiritualization which placed the believers in a close community with these potencies.*” $^2$ So close, indeed, that the Hierarchies of these Potencies, or Forces, have been classified on a graduated scale of seven from the ponderable to the imponderable. They are <term>Septenary</term>, not as an artificial aid to facilitate their comprehension, but in their real Cosmic gradation, from their chemical or physical composition to their purely spiritual composition. They are Gods to the ignorant masses—Gods independent and supreme—and Demons to the fanatics, who, as intellectual as they may often be, are unable to understand the spirit of the philosophical sentence, *in pluribus unum* [one in many, unity in diversity]. To the Hermetic philosopher, they are FORCES that are relatively “blind” or “intelligent,” depending on which of their principles he deals with. It took many millennia before they were finally, in our cultured age, degraded into simple chemical elements.

At any rate, good Christians, and especially Biblical Protestants, ought to show more reverence for the Four Elements if they wish to maintain any for Moses. For the *Bible* demonstrates the consideration and mystic significance in which the Hebrew Lawgiver held them on every page of the *Pentateuch*. Josephus shows it built in white, the color of Ether. Where did the Four Elements and the <term>Malachim</term> of the Hebrews come from? Whether their symbols originated on the shores of the Oxus, on the burning sands of Upper Egypt, or in the weird and glacial wild forests that cover the slopes and peaks of the sacred snowy mountains of Thessaly, or again, in the pampas of America—their symbols, we repeat, are always the same when traced to their source. Whether Egyptian or Pelasgian, <term>Âryan</term> or Semitic, the <term>Genius Loci</term> (the Local God) embraced all of Nature in its unity, but not specifically the four elements any more than one of their creations, such as trees, rivers, mountains, or stars. The <term>Genius Loci</term>—a very late afterthought of the last sub-races of the <term>Fifth Root-Race</term>, when the primitive and grand meaning had been nearly lost—was always the representative, through his accumulated titles, of all his colleagues. He was the God of *Fire*, symbolized by thunder, such as Jove or <term>Agni</term>; the God of *Water*, symbolized by the river bull or some sacred river or fountain, such as <term>Varuna</term>, Neptune, etc.; the God of *Air*, manifesting in the hurricane and tempest, such as <term>Vâyu</term> and <term>Indra</term>; and the God or Spirit of the *Earth*, who appeared in earthquakes, like Pluto, <term>Yama</term>, and many others.

These were the <term>Cosmic Gods</term>, always synthesizing everything into one, as found in every cosmogony or mythology. Thus, the Greeks had their Dodonean Jupiter, who included within himself the four Elements and the four cardinal points, and who was recognized, therefore, in old Rome under the pantheistic title of *Jupiter Mundus*; and who now, in modern Rome, has become the *Deus Mundus*, the one Mundane God, who is made to swallow all others in the latest theology by the arbitrary decision of his special ministers.

For primitive religion was something better than a simple preoccupation with physical phenomena, as remarked by *Schelling*, and principles more elevated than we modern *Sadducees* know of "were hidden under the transparent veil of such merely natural divinities as thunder, the winds, and rain." The fourfold Jupiter, like the four-faced *Brahmâ*, the aerial, the lightning, the terrestrial, and the marine God—the lord and master of the four Elements—may stand as a representative for the great Cosmic Gods of every nation. Although assigning power over fire to *Hephæstus-Vulcan*, over the sea to *Poseidon-Neptune*, and over the Earth to *Pluto-Aidoneus*, the AERIAL Jove was still all of these; for ÆTHER, from the beginning, had pre-eminence over and was the synthesis of all the Elements.

# THE FOUR ELEMENTS

Tradition tells of a grotto, a vast cave in the deserts of Central Asia, into which light pours through four seemingly natural apertures, or clefts placed crosswise at the four cardinal points. From noon until an hour before sunset, the light streams in—of four different colors, as is claimed: red, blue, orange-gold, and white—owing to conditions of either natural or artificially prepared vegetation and soil. The light converges in the center around a pillar of white marble with a globe upon it, which represents our earth. It is named the "Grotto of Zarathushtra."

Included among the arts and sciences of the Fourth Race, the Atlanteans, the phenomenal manifestation of the Four Elements—which these believers justly attributed to the intelligent interference of the Cosmic Gods—assumed a scientific character. The *Magic* of the ancient priests consisted, in those days, of addressing *their Gods in their own language*.

> *The speech of the men of the Earth cannot reach the Lords. Each must be addressed in the language of his respective Element.*

So says *The Book of Rules*, in a sentence that will be shown to be pregnant with meaning, adding as an explanation of the nature of that *Element-language*:

It is composed of SOUNDS, not words; of sounds, numbers, and figures. He who knows how to blend the three will call forth the response of the superintending Power <note>the Regent-God of the specific Element needed</note>.

Thus, this "language" is that of incantations or of MANTRAS, as they are called in India; sound is the most potent and effectual magic agent, and the first of the keys that opens the door of communication between Mortals and the Immortals. He who believes in the words and teachings of St. Paul has no right to pick out from the latter only those sentences which he chooses to accept while rejecting others; and St. Paul teaches most undeniably the existence of Cosmic Gods and their presence among us. Paganism preached a dual and simultaneous evolution, a "creation" *spiritualem ac mundanum* <note>spiritual and earthly</note>, as the Roman Church has it, ages before the advent of that Roman Church. Exoteric phraseology has changed little with respect to Divine Hierarchies since the greatest days of Paganism, or "Idolatry." Names alone have changed, along with claims that have now become false pretenses. For when, for instance, Plato put into the mouth of the Highest Principle "Father Ether," or Jupiter, the words, "the Gods of the Gods of whom I am the *maker* (opifex), as I am the father of all their works (*operumque parens*)," he knew the spirit of this sentence as fully, we suspect, as St. Paul did when saying: "For though there be those that are called Gods, whether in Heaven or on Earth, as there be Gods..."

Nor was it "superstitious" for the Greek Pagans to listen to the Oracle of Delphi when, at the approach of the fleet of Xerxes, that oracle advised them to "sacrifice to the winds," if the same must be regarded as *Divine Worship* among the Israelites, who sacrificed just as often to the wind and especially to the fire. The above is not a defense of Pagan Gods, nor is it an attack on the Christian Deity, nor does it mean belief in either. The writer is quite impartial and rejects the testimony in favor of both, neither praying to, believing in, nor dreading any such “personal” and anthropomorphic God. The parallels are brought forward simply as one more curious exhibition of the illogical and blind fanaticism of the civilized theologian. For, so far, there is not a very great difference between the two beliefs, and there is none in their respective effects upon morality or spiritual nature. The “light of Christ” shines upon features of the animal man just as hideous now as the “light of Lucifer” did in days of old. Says the missionary Lavoisier, of Cochin, in the *Journal des Colonies*:

> These unfortunate heathens in their superstition regard even the Elements as something that has comprehension! They still have faith in their idol Vâyu—the God or, rather, Demon of the Wind and Air; they firmly believe in the efficacy of their prayers, and in the powers of their Brâhmans over the winds and storms.

The logical and irrepressible conclusion arising from the parallels brought forward, and the denunciation of the missionary, is that the *commands* of the Brâhmans to their Element-Gods *not remaining* “ineffectual,” the power of the Brâhmans is thus placed on a par with that of Jesus. Moreover, Astarte is shown to be not a bit weaker in potency than the “Virgin of the Sea” of Christian sailors. But, as just remarked, the tree must be judged by its fruit. And once Christians are shown to be as immoral and as wicked as the Pagans ever were, what benefit has humanity derived from its change of gods and idols?

What God and the Christian Saints are justified in doing becomes a crime in ordinary mortals if they are successful. Sorcery and incantations are now regarded as fables; yet from the *Institutes of Justinian* down to the laws of England and America against witchcraft—obsolete but not repealed to this day—such incantations, even when only suspected, were punished as criminal acts. Why punish a fantasy? And yet we still read of Constantine the Emperor sentencing the philosopher Sopatrus to death for *unchaining the winds* and thus preventing ships laden with grain from arriving in time to end a famine. Pausanias is mocked when he claims that he saw with his own eyes "*men who by simple prayers and incantations*" stopped a heavy hailstorm. This does not prevent modern Christian writers from advising prayer during storms and danger and believing in its effectiveness. Hoppo and Stadlein, two magicians and sorcerers, were sentenced to death for "throwing charms on fruit" and transferring a harvest by magic arts from one field to another hardly a century ago, if we can believe Sprenger, the famous writer who vouches for it: "*Qui fruges excantassent segetem pellicentes incantando.*" <note>Who enchanted the fruits and drew away the crops by their magic.</note>

Let us close by reminding the reader that, without the slightest shadow of superstition, one may believe in the dual nature of every object on Earth—in spiritual and material, in visible and invisible Nature. Science virtually proves this while denying its own evidence. For if, as Sir William Grove says, the electricity we handle is but the result of ordinary matter affected by something invisible—the "*ultimate generating power*" of every Force, the "*one omnipresent influence*"—then it only becomes natural that one should believe as the Ancients did: namely, that every Element is dual in its nature. "ETHEREAL Fire is the emanation of the Kabir proper; the *aerial* is but the union (correlation) of the former with terrestrial fire, and its guidance and application on our earthly plane belongs to a *Kabir* of a lesser dignity"—an Elemental, perhaps, as an Occultist would call it; and the same may be said of every Cosmic Element.

No one will deny that the human being possesses various forces—magnetic, sympathetic, antipathetic, nervous, dynamic, occult, mechanical, mental, in fact, every kind of force—and that the physical forces are all biological in their essence, seeing that they intermingle with, and often merge into, those forces that we have named intellectual and moral, the first being

## SECTION 15

### ON KWAN-SHI-YIN AND KWAN-YIN

LIKE Avalokiteshvara, Kwan-Shi-Yin has passed through several transformations, but it is an error to say of him that he is a modern invention of the Northern Buddhists; for under another name, he has been known from the earliest times. **THE SECRET DOCTRINE** teaches that: “He who is the first to appear at Renovation will be the last to come before Re-absorption <note>Pralaya</note>.” Thus the Logos of all nations—from the Vedic Vishvakarman of the Mysteries down to the Savior of the present civilized nations—is the “Word” who was in the “Beginning” (or the re-awakening of the energizing Powers of Nature), with the ONE ABSOLUTE Born of Fire and Water, before these became distinct Elements. It was the “Maker,” the fashioner or modeler, of all things. “Without him was not anything made that was made. In him was life, and the life was the light of men,” who finally may be called, as he ever has been, the Alpha and the Omega of Manifested Nature. “The great Dragon of Wisdom is born of Fire and Water, and into Fire and Water will all be re-absorbed with him.” <note>Fa-hwa-King</note> As this Bodhisattva is said “to assume any form he pleases,” from the beginning of a Manvantara to its end—though his special birthday, or memorial day, is celebrated according to the Kin-kwang-ming-King, or “Luminous Sûtra of Golden Light,” in the second month on the nineteenth day, and that of “Maitreya Buddha,” in the first month on the first day—yet the two are one. He will appear as Maitreya Buddha, the last of the Avatars and Buddhas, in the Seventh Race. This belief and expectation are universal throughout the East. Only it is not in the Kali Yuga, our present terrifically materialistic age of Darkness, the “Black Age,” that a new Savior of Humanity can ever appear. The Kali Yuga is “the Golden Age” (!) only in the *mystic* writings of some French pseudo-Occultists. <note>See The Mission of the Jews</note>

Hence the ritual in the exoteric worship of this Deity was founded on magic. The Mantras are all taken from special books kept secret by the

Kwan-Shi-Yin is Avalokiteshvara, and both are forms of the Seventh Universal Principle; while in its highest metaphysical character, this Deity is the synthetic aggregation of all the Planetary Spirits, or Dhyân Chohans. He is the “Self-Manifested”; in short, the “Son of the Father.” Crowned with seven dragons, above his statue there appears the inscription *Pu-tsi-k'iun-ling*, “the universal Savior of all living beings.”

Of course, the name given in the archaic volume of the STANZAS is quite different, but Kwan-Yin is a perfect equivalent. In a temple of P'u-to, the sacred island of the Buddhists in China, Kwan-Shi-Yin is represented floating on a black aquatic bird (Kâlahamsa) and pouring the elixir of life onto the heads of mortals. As it flows, this elixir is transformed into one of the chief Dhyâni-Buddhas, the Regent of a star called the “Star of Salvation.” In his third transformation, Kwan-Yin is the informing Spirit or Genius of Water. In China, the Dalai Lama is believed to be an incarnation of Kwan-Shi-Yin, who in his third terrestrial appearance was a Bodhisattva, while the Teshu Lama is an incarnation of Amitâbha Buddha, or Gautama.

The former discovers “the old phallic gods, represented under two evident symbols, the *Kheen* or *Yang*, which is the *membrum virile* <note>male sexual organ</note>, and the *Khw-an* or *Yin*, the *pudendum muliebre* <note>female sexual organ</note>, or *Yom*.” ¹ Such a rendering seems all the more strange because Kwan-Shi-Yin (Avalokiteshvara) and Kwan-Yin, besides being the patron Deities of the Buddhist ascetics—the Yogis of Tibet—are the Gods of chastity. In their esoteric meaning, they are not even what is implied in the rendering of Mr. Rhys Davids’ *Buddhism*: “The name Avalokiteshvara . . . means ‘the Lord who looks down from on high.’” ² Nor is Kwan-Shi-Yin the “Spirit of the Buddhas present in the Church”; instead, literally interpreted, it means “the Lord that is seen.” In one sense, it is “the Divine SELF perceived by Self”—the human Self—that is, the Âtman or Seventh Principle, merged in the Universal, perceived by (or the object of perception to) Buddhi, the Sixth Principle, or Divine Soul in man. In a still higher sense, Avalokiteshvara = Kwan-Shi-Yin, referred to as the seventh Universal Principle, is the Logos perceived by the Universal Buddhi, or Soul, as the synthetic aggregate of the Dhyâni-Buddhas. He is not the “Spirit of Buddha present in the Church,” but the Omnipresent Universal Spirit manifested in the temple of the Cosmos or Nature. This Orientalist etymology of—

He is called the "Dragon of Wisdom" in STANZA 3, because all the *Logoi* of all the ancient religious systems are connected with, and symbolized by, serpents. In old Egypt, the God Nahbkoon, "he who unites the doubles," was represented as a serpent on human legs, either with or without arms. This was the Astral Light reuniting the Divine-Human to its purely Divine Monad—the Prototype in "Heaven" or Nature—through its dual physiological and spiritual power. It was the emblem of the resurrection of Nature; of Christ among the Ophites; and of Jehovah as the brazen serpent healing those who looked at him. The serpent was also an emblem of Christ for the Templars, as is shown by the Templar degree in Masonry. The symbol of Knooph (also Khnoom), or the Soul of the World, says Champollion, "is represented among other forms as a huge serpent on human legs; this reptile, being the emblem of the Good Genius and the true Agathodæmon, is sometimes bearded."⁵ This sacred animal is thus identical with the serpent of the Ophites and is depicted on a great number of engraved stones called Gnostic or Basilidean gems. Therefore, since the symbolic formula attempts to characterize that which is above scientific reasoning and is often far beyond our intellects, it must necessarily go beyond that intellect in some form or another, or else it will fade from human remembrance.

# ADDENDA

## ON OCCULTISM AND SCIENCE

### SECTION 1

#### REASONS FOR THESE ADDENDA

MANY of the doctrines contained in the preceding seven STANZAS and Commentaries having been studied and critically examined by some Western Theosophists, certain of the Occult Teachings have been found lacking from the ordinary standpoint of modern scientific knowledge. They seemed to encounter insurmountable difficulties in being accepted, and to require reconsideration in light of scientific criticism. Some friends have already been tempted to regret the necessity of so often questioning the assertions of modern Science. It appeared to them—and I only repeat their arguments here—that “to go against the teachings of its most eminent representatives was to invite a premature defeat in the eyes of the Western World.”

It is, therefore, desirable to define, once and for all, the position which the writer, who does not agree with her friends on this point, intends to maintain. So far as Science remains what in the words of Prof. T. H. Huxley it is, *namely*, “organized common sense,” so far as its inferences are drawn from accurate premises, and its generalizations rest on a purely inductive basis, every Theosophist and Occultist respectfully welcomes its contributions to the domain of cosmological law with due admiration. There can be no possible conflict between the teachings of Occult and so-called exact Science, wherever the conclusions of the latter are grounded on a foundation of unassailable fact. It is only when its more ardent representatives, overstepping the limits of observed phenomena in order to penetrate into the mysteries of Being, attempt to wrest the formation of Kosmos and its *living* Forces from

And now Occultism puts this question to Science: Is light a substance, or is it not? To know what light is, and whether it is an actual substance or a mere vibration of the "ethereal medium," Science must first learn what Matter, Atoms, Ether, and Force really are. The truth is, Science *knows nothing about any of these*, and it admits it. It has not even agreed on what to believe, as dozens of hypotheses on the same subject—coming from various and very eminent scientists—are antagonistic to each other and often self-contradictory. Thus, their learned speculations may, with a stretch of goodwill, be accepted as "working hypotheses" in a secondary sense, as Stallo puts it. But because they are fundamentally inconsistent with each other, they must eventually end by destroying one another. As declared by the author of *Concepts of Modern Physics*:

> It must not be forgotten that the several departments of science are simply arbitrary divisions of science as a whole. In these several departments, the same physical object may be considered under different aspects. The physicist may study its molecular relations, while the chemist determines its atomic constitution. But when they both deal with the same element or agent, it cannot have one set of properties in physics and another set contradictory to them in chemistry. If the physicist and chemist alike assume the existence of ultimate atoms that are absolutely unchanging in size and weight, the atom cannot be a cube or <term>oblate spheroid</term> for physical purposes and a sphere for chemical purposes. And a group of constant atoms cannot be a collection of spatially extended and absolutely inert and impenetrable masses in a crucible or retort, and then a system of mere centers of force as part of a magnet or of a <term>Clamond battery</term>. The universal ether cannot be soft and mobile to please the chemist and rigid-elastic to satisfy the physicist; it cannot be continuous at the command of Sir William Thomson and discontinuous on the suggestion of Cauchy or Fresnel. ¹

Regarding the atom, one has a right to expect to find a similar unanimity in the qualities assigned to this unique entity, the foundation of all that exists. The inevitable result is the existing subdivision of our sciences, each of which, in its own little isolated category, constructs an atom that satisfies the requirements of the phenomena it studies, without being at all concerned about the requirements proper to the phenomena of the neighboring category. The metaphysician dismisses the principles of attraction and repulsion as dreams; the mathematician, who analyzes the laws of elasticity and those of the propagation of light, admits them implicitly, without even naming them. There is no agreement even within one and the same science as to the properties of the atom. Each constructs an atom to suit his own fancy, in order to explain some special phenomenon with which he is particularly concerned.¹

Newton’s innermost thoughts and ideas were perverted, and only the mere physical shell of his great mathematical learning was utilized.

Science is honeycombed with metaphysics;¹ its most fundamental principles, while inseparably wedded to transcendentalism, are nevertheless—in order to show modern science is divorced from such "dreams"—distorted and often ignored in the maze of contradictory theories and hypotheses. A very strong confirmation of this charge lies in the fact that science finds itself absolutely compelled to accept the "hypothetical" Ether, yet tries to explain it on the materialistic basis of atomo-mechanical laws. A second proof is found in the many contradictory statements made about the atom—the most metaphysical object in creation.

Now, what does the modern science of physics know of Ether? The first concept of it belongs undeniably to ancient philosophers; the Greeks borrowed it from the Aryans, and the origin of modern Ether is found in—though disfigured from—<term>AKASHA</term>. This disfigurement is claimed to be a modification and refinement of the idea of Lucretius. Let us then examine the modern concept using several scientific volumes containing the admissions of the physicists themselves.

As Stallo shows, the existence of Ether is accepted in physical astronomy, in ordinary physics, and in chemistry.

By astronomers, this ether was originally regarded as a fluid of extreme thinness and mobility, offering no noticeable resistance to the motions of celestial bodies; the question of its continuity or discontinuity was not seriously debated. Its main function in modern astronomy has been to serve as a basis for hydrodynamical theories.

Next, in order to explain the dispersion and polarization of light, physicists had to resort once more to their "scientific imagination," and immediately endowed the Ether with (a) an atomic or molecular structure, and (b) an enormous elasticity, "so that its resistance to deformation far exceeded that of the most rigid elastic bodies." This necessitated the theory of the *essential discontinuity of matter*, and hence of Ether. After having accepted this discontinuity in order to account for dispersion and polarization, theoretical impossibilities were discovered regarding such dispersion. Cauchy’s "scientific imagination" saw atoms as "material points without extension," and he proposed—in order to overcome the most formidable obstacles to the undulatory theory (namely, some well-known mechanical theorems that stood in the way)—to assume that the ethereal medium of propagation, instead of being continuous, should consist of particles separated by noticeable distances. Fresnel provided the same service to the phenomena of polarization. E. B. Hunt upset the theories of both.² There are now men of science who proclaim them "materially fallacious," while others—the "atomo-mechanicalists"—cling to them with desperate tenacity. The supposition of an *atomic* or *molecular* constitution of Ether is further upset by thermodynamics, for Clerk Maxwell showed that such a medium would be simply a gas.³ The hypothesis of "finite intervals" is thus proven useless as a supplement to the undulatory theory. Besides, eclipses fail to reveal any such variation of color as is supposed by Cauchy, on the assumption that the chromatic rays are propagated with different velocities. Astronomy has pointed out more than one phenomenon absolutely at variance with this doctrine.

Thus, while in one department of physics the *atomo-molecular* constitution of the Ether is accepted in order to account for one special set of phenomena, in another department such a constitution is found to be quite subversive to a number of well-ascertained facts, and Hirn’s charges are thus justified. Chemistry deemed it *impossible* to concede the enormous elasticity of the ether without depriving it of those properties upon which its usefulness in the construction of chemical theories mainly depended.

# SECTION 3

## IS GRAVITATION A LAW?

The corpuscular theory has been unceremoniously put aside, but gravitation—the principle that all bodies attract each other with a force directly proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the squares of the distances between them—survives to this day and reigns as supreme as ever in the alleged ethereal waves of Space. As a hypothesis, it has been threatened with death due to its inadequacy in embracing all the facts presented to it; as a *physical law*, it is the King of the late and once all-potent "Imponderables." "It is little short of blasphemy . . . . an insult to Newton’s grand memory to doubt it!"—is the exclamation of an American reviewer of *Isis Unveiled*. Well; what, finally, is that *invisible and intangible* God in whom we should believe with blind faith? Astronomers, who see in gravitation an easy solution for many things and a *universal* force that allows them to calculate planetary motions, care little about the Cause of Attraction. They call Gravity a law, a *cause* in itself. We call the forces acting under that name effects, and very secondary *effects*, too. One day it will be found that the scientific hypothesis does not suffice after all, and then it will follow the corpuscular theory of light and be consigned to rest for many scientific eons in the archives of all exploded speculations. Has Newton himself not expressed grave doubts about the nature of Force and the physical reality of the "Agents," as they were then called? So has Cuvier, another scientific light shining in the night of research. He warns his readers, in the *Révolution du Globe*, about the doubtful nature of the so-called Forces, saying that "it is not so certain whether those agents were not, after all, Spiritual Powers [*des agents spirituels*]." At the beginning of his *Principia*, Sir Isaac Newton took the greatest care to impress upon his school that he did not use the word "attraction" in a physical sense regarding the mutual action of bodies. To him, he said, it was a purely mathematical conception, involving no consideration of real

### CURRENT HYPOTHESES EXPLAINING THE ORIGIN OF ROTATION

Rotation has originated:
(a) By the collision of nebular masses wandering aimlessly in space, or by *attraction* "in cases where no actual impact occurs."

For, if Science sometimes succeeds, with great ingenuity, in explaining some of such stoppages, retrograde motions, angles outside the orbits, etc., as appearances resulting from the inequality of their progress and ours in the course of our mutual and respective orbits, we still know that there are others, and "very real and considerable deviations," according to Herschel, "which cannot be explained except by the mutual and irregular action of those planets and by the perturbing influence of the sun."

We understand, however, that there are, besides those little and accidental perturbations, continuous perturbations called "secular"—because of the extreme slowness with which the irregularity increases and affects the relations of the elliptic movement—and that these perturbations *can* be corrected. From Newton, who found that this world needed *repairing* very often, down to Reynaud, all say the same. In his *Terre et Ciel* (Earth and Heaven), the latter says:

> The orbits described by the planets are far from immutable, and are, on the contrary, subject to a perpetual mutation in their position and form <note>5. P. 28</note>

Proving gravitation and the *peripatetic laws* to be as negligent as they are quick to repair their mistakes. The charge as it stands seems to be that:

> These orbits are alternately widening and narrowing, their great axis lengthens and diminishes, or oscillates at the same time from right to left around the sun, the plane itself, in which they are situated, raising and lowering itself periodically while pivoting around itself with a kind of tremor.
