## THE MASKS OF SCIENCE

### PHYSICS OR METAPHYSICS?

If there is anything like progress on earth, Science will one day have to give up, willingly or unwillingly, such monstrous ideas as its physical, self-guiding laws, void of Soul and Spirit, and will then have to turn to the Occult Teachings. It has already done so, however much the title pages and revised editions of the *Scientific Catechism* may be altered. It has now been over half a century since, in comparing modern with ancient thought, it was found that, however different our philosophy may appear from that of our ancestors, it is nevertheless composed only of *additions* and *subtractions* taken from the old philosophy and transmitted drop by drop through the filter of what came before.

This fact was well known to Faraday and to other eminent men of science. Atoms, Ether, and Evolution itself—all come to modern Science from ancient notions; all are based on the conceptions of the archaic nations. Heat and light are against occult doctrines. But it is not enough for men of science, or their defenders, to say that they do not deny dynamic power to *light and heat*, and to urge as proof the fact that Mr. Crookes’ radiometer has not unsettled any views. If they wish to fathom the ultimate nature of these forces, they must first admit their *substantial* nature, however supersensory that nature may be. Neither do occultists deny the correctness of the vibratory theory. <note>1</note> They only limit its functions to our Earth—declaring its inadequacy on planes other than ours, since Masters of the occult sciences perceive the causes that produce ethereal vibrations. If all these were only the fictions of the alchemists, or the dreams of the mystics, then men such as Paracelsus, Philalethes, Van Helmont, and so many others would have to be regarded as worse than visionaries; they would become impostors and deliberate mystifiers.

Occultists are criticized for calling the *cause* of light, heat, sound, cohesion, magnetism, and so on, a *substance*. <note>2</note> Mr. Clerk Maxwell has stated that the pressure of strong sunlight on a square mile is about 3 1/4 lbs. It is, they are told, “the energy of the myriad ether waves”; and when they call it a substance striking that area, their explanation is proclaimed *unscientific*.

There is no justification for such an accusation. In no way—as already stated more than once—do occultists dispute the explanations of science as providing a solution for the *immediate* objective agencies at work. Science only errs in believing that, because it has detected the *proximate* cause of these phenomena in vibratory waves, it has therefore revealed EVERYTHING that lies beyond the threshold of sense. It merely traces the sequence of phenomena on a plane of effects—illusory projections from the region that occultism has long since penetrated. And the latter maintains that those etheric tremors are not created, as science asserts, by the vibrations of the molecules of known bodies—the matter of our terrestrial objective consciousness—but that we must seek for the ultimate causes of light, heat, and so on, in MATTER existing in supersensory states. These states, however, are as fully objective to the spiritual eye of man as a horse or a tree is to an ordinary mortal. Light and heat are the ghost or shadow of matter in motion. Such states can be perceived by the seer.

Conceptions of force are summarized by our conceptions of this, that, or another mode of motion. Force is thus simply the transition of one state of motion into another state of the same: of electricity into heat and light, of heat into sound or some mechanical function, and so on.<note>On the plane of manifestation and illusory matter, it may be so; yet it is not merely that, for it is vastly more.</note> The first time electric fluid was produced by man on earth, it must have been by friction; hence, as is well known, it is heat that produces it by disturbing its zero state,<note>Neutral, or <term>Laya</term>.</note> and electricity exists no more on earth *per se* than heat or light or any other force. When electricity decomposes water or heats a platinum wire, we speak of the force of the electric fluid. When the rays of the sun are intercepted by the thermometer bulb and its mercury expands, we speak of the calorific energy of the sun. In short, when one state of a determined quantity of motion ceases, another state of motion equivalent to the preceding takes its place, and the result of such transformation or correlation is—force. In all cases where such a transformation, or the passage of one state of motion into another, is entirely absent, no force is possible. Let us admit for a moment an absolutely homogeneous state of the universe, and our conception of force falls to nothing.

Therefore, it becomes evident that the force which materialism considers as the cause of the diversity that surrounds us is, in sober reality, only an effect—a result of that diversity. From such a point of view, force is not the cause of motion, but a result, while the cause of that force, or forces, is not substance or matter, but motion itself. Matter must thus be set aside, and with it the basic principle of materialism, which has become unnecessary; since force reduced to a state of motion can give no idea of substance. If force is the result of motion, then it becomes incomprehensible why that motion should bear witness to matter and not to spirit or a spiritual essence. True, our reason cannot conceive of a motion without something moving (and our reason is right), but the nature or *esse* [essence] of that something moving remains entirely unknown to science. A materialist has no special privileges in this instance, nor can he claim any. The law of the conservation of energy, as seen here, is shown to be illegitimate in its pretensions and claims in this case. The "great dogma"—*no force without matter and no matter without force*—falls to the ground and entirely loses the solemn significance with which materialism has tried to invest it. The conception of force still gives no idea of matter and in no way compels us to see it as "the origin of all origins."<note>*Scientific Letters*, Professor A. Butlerof.</note>

> See now the curious contradiction into which this fundamental principle is leading the Materialists. The atom is *indivisible*, and at the same time, we know it to be *elastic*. An attempt to deprive it of elasticity is unthinkable; it would amount to an absurdity. Absolutely non-elastic atoms could never exhibit even one of those numerous phenomena that are attributed to their correlations. Without any elasticity, the atoms could not manifest their energy, and the Substance of the Materialists would remain stripped of every force. Therefore, if the Universe is composed of atoms, then those atoms *must be elastic*. It is here that we meet with an insuperable obstacle. For what are the conditions required for the manifestation of elasticity? An elastic ball, when striking against an obstacle, is flattened and contracts, which would be impossible if the ball did not consist of particles whose relative positions temporarily change at the moment of impact. This may be said of elasticity in general; no elasticity is possible without a change in the position of the component particles of an elastic body. This means that the elastic body is changeable and consists of particles; or, in other words, that elasticity can belong only to those bodies that are divisible. And yet, the atom is elastic.²

But doing this requires a boundless love of truth and the surrender of that prestige—however false—of *infallibility* that men of science have gained among the ignorant and flighty, though cultured, masses of the uninitiated. The blending of the two sciences, the *archaic* and the *modern*, requires first of all the abandonment of current *materialistic* approaches. It necessitates a kind of religious mysticism and even the study of ancient magic, which our academics will never pursue. This necessity is easily explained. Just as the real meaning of the substances and elements mentioned in old alchemical works is hidden beneath the most ridiculous metaphors, so too are the physical, psychic, and spiritual natures of the elements (such as *fire*) hidden in the <term>Vedas</term>, and especially in the <term>Puranas</term>, under allegories understandable only to initiates. If they had no meaning, then indeed all these long legends and allegories about the sacredness of the three types of fire, and the *forty-nine original fires*—personified by the sons of Daksha’s daughters and the <term>Rishis</term>, their husbands, “who with the first son of <term>Brahma</term> and his three descendants constitute the forty-nine fires”—would be nothing more than idiotic nonsense. But this is not the case. Every *fire* has a distinct function and meaning in both the physical and spiritual worlds. Furthermore, in its essential nature, it has a corresponding relationship to one of the human psychic faculties, in addition to its well-defined chemical and physical powers when interacting with terrestrially differentiated matter. It thus acts *through ponderable matter*. If universal space were filled with caloric or sun-force alone (without ponderable matter), caloric would also be inactive and would constitute a boundless ocean of powerless or inactive ether. This is because it would then have nothing on which to act, while ponderable matter—however inactive by itself—has "certain properties by which it modifies and controls the actions of caloric, both of which are governed by unchanging laws that have their origin in the mutual relations and specific properties of each."

And he lays down a law which he believes is absolute, and which is expressed as follows:

> "Through the attraction of caloric for ponderable matter, it unites and holds all things together; through its self-repulsive energy, it separates and expands all things."

# SECTION 7

## LIFE, FORCE, OR GRAVITY

THE *imponderable* fluids have had their day; "mechanical Forces" are less talked about. Science has put on a new face for this last quarter of a century, but gravitation has remained, owing its survival to new combinations after the old ones had nearly killed it. It may satisfy scientific hypotheses quite well, but the question is whether it corresponds as well to truth and represents a fact in nature. Attraction by itself is *not* sufficient to explain even planetary motion; how, then, can it presume to explain the rotatory motion in the infinite reaches of Space? Attraction alone will never fill all the gaps unless a special impulse is admitted for every sidereal body, and the rotation of every planet with its satellites is shown to be due to some *one cause* combined with attraction. And even then, says an Astronomer <note>*Natural Philosophy*, article 142</note>, Science would have to name that cause.

Occultism has named it for ages, as have all the ancient Philosophers; but now, all such beliefs are proclaimed to be exploded superstitions. The "extra-cosmic" God has killed every possibility of belief in *intra-cosmic* intelligent Forces; yet who, or what, is the original *pusher* in that motion? Francœur asks: <note>*Astronomy*, page 342</note>

When we have learned the cause—*unique and special*—that pushes, we will be ready to combine it with the one which attracts.

And again:

> Attraction between the celestial bodies is only repulsion; it is the sun that drives them incessantly onward, for otherwise, their motion would stop.

If this theory of the Sun-Force being the primary cause of all life on earth and of all motion in heaven is ever accepted, and if that other, far bolder theory of Herschel—regarding certain organisms in the Sun—is accepted even as a provisional hypothesis, then our teachings will be vindicated. Esoteric allegory will be shown to have anticipated modern Science by millions of years, probably; for such are the Archaic Teachings. Mârtanda, the Sun, watches.

In all structures that possess the capacity for movement and sensation, the nervous ether passes into all such parts; and since the nervous ether is, in my view, a direct product of the blood, we may look upon it as a part of the atmosphere of the blood.

The evidence in favor of the existence of an elastic medium pervading the nervous matter and capable of being influenced by simple pressure is entirely convincing.

In nervous structure there is, unquestionably, a true nervous fluid, just as our predecessors taught. <margin>¹ Paracelsus, for one, who called it *Liquor Vitæ* and *Archæus*.</margin> The precise chemical (?) <margin>² Alchemical composition, rather.</margin> composition of this fluid is not yet well known; its physical characteristics have been little studied. We do not know whether it moves in currents; we do not know whether it circulates; we do not know whether it is formed in the centers and passes from them to the nerves, or whether it is formed everywhere that blood enters a nerve. Consequently, we do not know the exact uses of the fluid. It occurs to me, however, that the actual fluid of nervous matter is not itself sufficient to act as the subtle medium that connects the outer with the inner universe of humans and animals. I think—and this is the modification I suggest to the older theory—there must be another form of matter present during life; a matter which exists in the state of vapor or gas, which pervades the whole nervous organism, surrounds and is the medium of all motion communicated to and from the nervous centers. Once it is clearly presented to the mind that during life *there is in the animal body a finely diffused form of matter, a vapor filling every part—and even stored in some parts—a matter constantly renewed by vital chemistry, a matter as easily disposed of as the breath after it has served its purpose, a new flood of light breaks upon the intelligence.* <margin>³ "This vital force radiates around man like a luminous sphere," says Paracelsus in *Paragranum*.</margin> <margin>⁴ *Popular Science Review*, Vol. x, pp. 380-3.</margin>

We fail to see this, and we *know* it is not so. Pantheism *may* be “physically rediscovered.” It was known, perceived, and felt by the whole of antiquity. Pantheism manifests itself in the vast expanse of the starry heavens, in the breathing of the seas and oceans, and in the trembling life of the smallest blade of grass. Philosophy rejects a single *finite* and *imperfect* God in the universe—the human-like deity of the Monotheist as represented by his followers. It repudiates, in its name of *Philo-theo-sophia*, the grotesque idea that an Infinite, *Absolute* Deity should, or rather *could*, have any direct or indirect relation to the finite, illusory evolutions of Matter. Therefore, it cannot imagine a universe *outside* of that Deity, or the absence of that Deity from the smallest speck of animate or inanimate Substance. [This does not mean that every bush, tree, or stone is God or a god, but only that every speck of the manifested material of the <term>Kosmos</term> belongs to, and is the Substance of “God,” however low it may have fallen in its cyclic rotation through the Eternities of the Ever-Becoming. It also means that every such speck individually, and the <term>Kosmos</term> collectively, is an aspect and a reminder of that universal *One Soul*—which Philosophy refuses to call God, as doing so limits the eternal and ever-present root and essence.]

Why either the Ether of Space or “Nervous Ether” should “destroy the individuality of every sense” seems incomprehensible to one acquainted with the real nature of that “Nervous Ether” under its <term>Sanskrit</term>, or rather Esoteric and Kabbalistic name. Dr. Richardson agrees that—

> If we did not individually produce the medium of communication between ourselves and the outer world—if it were produced from the outside and adapted to only one kind of vibration—then fewer senses would be required than we actually possess. To take only two illustrations: the ether of light is not adapted for sound, yet we hear as well as see; while air, the medium for the movement of sound, is not the medium for light, yet we see and hear.

This is not so. The opinion that Pantheism “fails to be true because it would destroy the individuality of every individual sense” shows that all the conclusions of the learned doctor are based on modern physical theories, even though he would like to reform them. But he will find it impossible to do this unless he allows for the existence of spiritual senses to replace the gradual atrophy of the physical ones. “We see and hear” (at least in Dr. Richardson’s mind) in accordance with the explanations of the phenomena of sight and hearing provided by that same Materialistic Science which claims that we cannot see and hear in any other way. The Occultists and Mystics know better.

The <term>Vedic Aryans</term> were as familiar with the mysteries of sound and color on the physical plane as our <term>physiologists</term> are, but they had also mastered the secrets of both on planes inaccessible to the <term>Materialists</term>. They knew of a double set of senses: spiritual and material. In a person who is deprived of one or more senses, the remaining senses become more developed; for instance, a blind person will recover sight through the senses of touch, hearing, etc., and one who is deaf will be able to "hear" through sight, by audibly seeing the words uttered by the lips and mouth of the speaker. But these are cases that still belong to the world of Matter. The spiritual senses—those that act on a higher plane of consciousness—are rejected from the start by physiology because it is ignorant of the <term>Sacred Science</term>. It limits the action of <term>Ether</term> to vibrations and, by separating it from air—even though air is simply differentiated and compound <term>Ether</term>—it forces it to perform functions that fit the specific theories of the physiologist. But there is more real science in the teachings of the <term>Upanishads</term>, when correctly understood, than the <term>Orientalists</term> (who do not understand them at all) are willing to admit. Mental as well as physical correlations of the seven senses—seven on the physical and seven on the mental planes—are clearly explained and defined in the <term>Vedas</term>, and especially in the <term>Anugîtâ</term>.

> The indestructible and the destructible: such is the double manifestation of the Self. Of these, the indestructible is the existent [the true essence or nature of Self, the underlying principles]; the manifestation as an individual entity is called the destructible. <gloss>¹</gloss>

Thus speaks the Ascetic in the <term>Anugîtâ</term>, and also:

> [Everyone who is twice-born (initiated) knows this is the teaching of the ancients.] Space is the first entity. Now Space [<term>Akasha</term>, or the <term>Noumenon</term> of <term>Ether</term>] has one quality, and that is stated to be sound only. [And the] qualities of sound [are] <term>Shadja</term>, <term>Rishabha</term>, together with <term>Gandhara</term>, <term>Madhyama</term>, <term>Panchama</term>, and beyond these [it should be understood, are] <term>Nishada</term> and <term>Dhaivata</term> [the Hindu scale]. <gloss>²</gloss>

These seven notes of the scale are the principles of sound. The qualities of every element, as of every sense, are sevenfold (septenary); to judge and dogmatize about them based on their manifestation on the material or objective plane—which is itself sevenfold—is quite arbitrary. For it is only by the Self emancipating itself from these seven causes of illusion that we can acquire knowledge (Secret Wisdom) of the qualities of sensory objects on their dual plane of manifestation: the visible and the invisible. Thus it is said:

> Hear me state this wonderful mystery. Hear also the exhaustive explanation of causes. The nose, and the tongue, and eye, and the skin, and the ear as

# THE SECRET DOCTRINE

Truly, then, one should study Occult Philosophy before one begins to seek for and verify the mysteries of Nature on its surface alone; for only he "who knows the truth about the qualities of Nature, who understands the creation of all entities . . . is emancipated" from error. The Preceptor says:

Accurately understanding the great (tree), of which the unperceived <note>Occult Nature, the root of all</note> is the sprout from the seed <note><term>Parabrahman</term></note>, which consists of the understanding <note><term>Mahat</term>, or the Universal Intelligent Soul</note> as its trunk; the branches of which are the great egoism;¹ in the hollows of which are the sprouts, namely, the senses; of which the great <note>occult, or invisible</note> elements are the flower-bunches;² the gross elements <note>the gross objective matter</note> are the smaller boughs, which are always possessed of leaves, always possessed of flowers; which is eternal and the seed of which is the Brahman <note>the Deity</note>; and cutting it with that excellent sword—knowledge <note>Secret Wisdom</note>—one attains immortality and casts off birth and death.³

This is the Tree of Life, the <term>Ashvattha</term> tree; only AFTER cutting it can MAN, the slave of life and death, be emancipated.

But the men of Science know nothing, nor will they hear of the "Sword of Knowledge" used by the Adepts and Ascetics. Hence the one-sided remarks of even the most liberal among them, based on and flowing from undue importance given to the arbitrary divisions and classification of Physical Science. Occultism heeds them very little, and Nature heeds them still less. The whole range of physical phenomena proceeds from the Primary Ether—<term>Âkâsha</term>, just as dual-natured <term>Âkâsha</term> proceeds from so-called undifferentiated Chaos; the latter is the primary aspect of <term>Mûlaprakriti</term>, the Root-Matter and the first abstract Idea one can form of <term>Parabrahman</term>. Modern Science may divide its hypothetically conceived Ether in as many ways as it likes; the real <term>Æther</term> of Space will remain as it is throughout. It has its seven "principles," as all the rest of Nature has; where there were no Ether, there would be no sound, as it is the vibrating sounding-board in Nature in all its seven differentiations. This is the first mystery the Initiates of old have learned.

Our present normal physical senses were, from our present point of view, abnormal in those days of slow and progressive downward evolution and the fall into Matter. And there was a time when all that is regarded as exceptional in our modern era—so puzzling to the Physiologists who are now compelled to believe in them, such as thought-transference, clairvoyance, clairaudience, etc.; in short, all that is now called "wonderful and abnormal"—when all that and much more belonged to the senses and faculties common to all humanity. We are, however, cycling back and cycling forward; that is, having lost in spirituality what we acquired in physical development until almost the end of

Where are we to draw the line between distinct existence and identity? No one doubts that oxygen, sodium, chlorine, and sulfur are separate elements; and when we come to such groups as chlorine, bromine, iodine, etc., we still feel no doubt. However, if degrees of “elementicity” were admissible—and we may ultimately have to come to that—it might be allowed that chlorine approximates much more closely to bromine than to oxygen, sodium, or sulfur. If we stir up the whole thoroughly so as to ensure a uniform mixture of the solution and the ammonia, and set the vessel aside for an hour, carefully excluding dust, we may still find the liquid clear and bright, without any vestige of turbidity. After three or four hours, however, an opalescence will declare itself, and the next morning a precipitate will have appeared. Now let us ask ourselves, what can be the meaning of this phenomenon? The quantity of precipitant added was insufficient to throw down more than half the yttria present; therefore a process akin to selection has been going on for several hours. The precipitation has evidently not been effected at random, those molecules of the base being decomposed which happened to come in contact with a corresponding molecule of ammonia; for we have taken care that the liquids should be uniformly mixed, so that one molecule of the original salt would not be more exposed to decomposition than any other. If, further, we consider the time which elapses before the appearance of a precipitate, we cannot avoid coming to the conclusion that the action which has been going on for the first few hours is of a selective character. The problem is not why a precipitate is produced, but what determines or directs some atoms to fall down and others to remain in solution? Out of the multitude of atoms present, what power is it that directs each atom to choose the proper path? We may picture to ourselves some directive force passing the atoms one by one in review, selecting one for precipitation and another for solution until all have been adjusted.

## THE COMING FORCE

### ITS POSSIBILITIES AND IMPOSSIBILITIES

Shall we say that Force is “moving Matter,” or “Matter in motion,” and a manifestation of Energy; or that Matter and Force are the phenomenal, differentiated aspects of the one primary, undifferentiated Cosmic Substance?

The compound molecules are in its power, but their atoms still elude its grasp. <term>Occultism</term> sees in all these Forces and manifestations a ladder: the lower rungs belong to exoteric Physics, and the higher are traced to a living, intelligent, invisible Power. This Power is, as a rule, the unconcerned—but in exceptional cases, the conscious—Cause of the sense-born phenomena designated as this or that natural law.

We say and maintain that SOUND is a tremendous occult power; it is a stupendous force, of which the electricity generated by a million Niagaras could never counteract even the smallest potential when directed with *Occult Knowledge*. Sound can be produced of such a nature that the Pyramid of Cheops could be raised into the air, or that a dying man—nay, one at his last breath—could be revived and filled with new energy and vigor.

For Sound generates, or rather attracts together, the elements that produce an ozone whose creation is beyond chemistry but within the limits of alchemy. It may even *resurrect* a person or an animal whose astral "vital body" has not been irreparably separated from the physical body by the breaking of the magnetic or odic cord. As *someone saved three times from death* by that power, the writer should be credited with personally knowing something about it.

And if all this appears too *unscientific* to even be noticed, let Science explain by what known mechanical and physical laws the recently produced phenomena of the so-called Keely motor occur. What is it that acts as the formidable generator of this invisible but tremendous force—a power that is not only capable of driving a 25-horsepower engine but has even been employed to physically lift the machinery? Yet this is done simply by drawing a fiddle bow across a tuning fork, as has been repeatedly proven. For the *etheric Force* discovered by John Worrell Keely of Philadelphia—well-known in America and Europe—is *no hallucination*. Notwithstanding his failure to utilize it—a failure predicted and maintained by some Occultists from the start—the phenomena shown by the discoverer during the last few years have been wonderful, almost miraculous; not in the sense of the *supernatural*¹ but of the *superhuman*. Had Keely been permitted to succeed, he might have reduced a whole army to atoms in the space of a few seconds as easily as he reduced a dead ox to that condition.

The reader is now asked to give serious attention to that newly discovered potency, which the discoverer has named "Inter-Etheric Force, and Forces."

If the chamber were hermetically sealed and strong enough, the vacuum surrounding the bell would be brought to a pressure of many thousands of pounds per square inch by the tenuous substance evolved. In my estimation, sound truly defined is the disturbance of atomic equilibrium, rupturing actual atomic corpuscles; and the substance thus released must certainly be a specific order of etheric flow. Under these conditions, is it unreasonable to suppose that if this flow were kept up and the body were thus robbed of its element, it would in time disappear entirely? All bodies—animal, vegetable, and mineral—are formed primitively from this highly tenuous ether, and they are only returned to their high gaseous condition when brought into a state of differential equilibrium. Regarding odor, we can only get some definite idea of its extreme and wondrous tenuity by considering that a large area of the atmosphere can be scented for many years from a single grain of musk, which, if weighed after that long interval, will be found not to have appreciably diminished. The great paradox accompanying the flow of odorous particles is that they can be held under confinement in a glass vessel.¹ Here is a substance of much higher tenuity than the glass that holds it, and yet it cannot escape. It is like a sieve with meshes large enough to pass marbles, yet holding fine sand which cannot pass through; in fact, it is a molecular vessel holding an atomic substance. This is a problem that would confound those who stop to acknowledge it. But as infinitely tenuous as odor is, it holds a very crude relation to the substance of subdivision that governs a magnetic flow (a flow of sympathy, if you would like to call it that). This subdivision comes next to sound, but is above sound. The action of a magnet's flow coincides somewhat with the receiving and distributing portion of the human brain, giving off at all times a decreasing ratio of the amount received. It is a grand illustration of the control of mind over matter, which gradually wears down the physical until dissolution takes place. By the same ratio, the magnet gradually loses its power and becomes inert. If the relations that exist between mind and matter could be balanced and maintained, we would live on in our physical state eternally, as there would be no physical decline. But this physical decline leads, at its end, to the source of a much higher development—namely, the liberation of pure ether from the crude molecular state, which, in my estimation, is much to be desired.²

As fully as we believe in these vibrations as the *proximate*, the *immediate* cause of such sensations, we just as absolutely reject the one-sided scientific theory that there is *no* factor to be considered external to us other than etheric or atmospheric vibrations.¹

There *is* a *transcendental* set of causes set in motion, so to speak, in the occurrence of these phenomena, which—*not being in relation to our narrow range of cognition*—can only be understood and traced to their source and their nature by the spiritual faculties of the Adept. They are, as Asclepios puts it to the King, "*incorporeal corporealities*," such as those that "*appear in the mirror*," and "*abstract forms*" that we see, *hear*, and *smell* in our dreams and visions. What do "modes of motion," light, and ether have to do with these? Yet we see, hear, smell, and touch them; therefore, they are as much *realities* to us in our dreams as any other thing on this plane of *Maya*.

The star under which a human Entity is born, says the Occult Teaching, will remain forever *its* star throughout the whole cycle of its incarnations in one Manvantara. But *this is not his astrological star*. The latter is concerned with and connected to the PERSONALITY, the former with the INDIVIDUALITY. The “Angel” of that Star, or the Dhyâni-Buddha connected with it, will be either the guiding or simply the presiding “Angel,” so to speak, in every new rebirth of the Monad, *which is part of his own essence*, though his vehicle, man, may remain forever ignorant of this fact. The Adepts each have their Dhyâni-Buddha, their elder “Twin-Soul,” and they know it, calling it “Father-Soul” and “Father-Fire.” It is only at the last and supreme Initiation, however, when placed face to face with the bright “Image,” that they learn to recognize it. How much did Bulwer Lytton know of this mystic fact when describing, in one of his highest inspirational moods, Zanoni face to face with his Augoeides?

The Logos, or both the unmanifested and the manifested Word, is called by the Hindus Îshvara, the Lord, though the Occultists give it another name.

As each planet can stand in relation to each of the others in twelve different aspects, their combinations must be almost infinite—as infinite, in fact, as the spiritual, psychic, mental, and physical capacities in the numberless varieties of the *genus homo*, each of which varieties is born under one of the seven planets and one of the said countless planetary combinations.¹]

# SECTION 11

## ANCIENT THOUGHT IN MODERN DRESS

MODERN *SCIENCE IS ANCIENT THOUGHT DISTORTED*, and nothing more. We have seen, however, *what intuitional scientists think* and are busy with; and now the reader shall be given a few more proofs of the fact that more than one Fellow of the Royal Society is unconsciously approaching the derided Secret Sciences.

With regard to Cosmogony and primeval matter, modern speculations are undeniably ancient thought, improved by contradictory theories of recent origin. The whole foundation belongs to Grecian and Indian Archaic Astronomy and Physics, which in those days were always called Philosophy. In all the Aryan and Greek speculations, we meet with the conception of an all-pervading, unorganized, and homogeneous Matter, or Chaos, renamed by modern scientists the “nebular condition of the world-stuff.” What Anaxagoras called Chaos in his *Homoiomeria* is now called “primitive fluid” by Sir W. Thomson. The Hindu and Greek atomists—<term>Kanâda</term>, <term>Leucippus</term>, <term>Democritus</term>, <term>Epicurus</term>, <term>Lucretius</term>, etc.—are now reflected, as in a clear mirror, in the supporters of the Atomic Theory of our modern days, beginning with <term>Leibniz’s Monads</term> and ending with the <term>Vortical Atoms</term> of Sir W. Thomson. <note>The Elemental Vortices inaugurated by the “Mind” have not been improved by their modern transformation.</note> True, the old corpuscular theory is rejected, and the undulatory theory has taken its place. <note>Science at present considers light to be both corpuscular and undulatory.</note> But the question is: *is the latter so firmly established that it is not liable to be dethroned like its predecessor?* Light, from its metaphysical aspect, has been fully treated in *Isis Unveiled*.

Light is the first-begotten and the first emanation of the Supreme, and Light is Life, says the Evangelist and the Kabalist. Both are electricity—the life principle, the <term>anima mundi</term>—pervading the universe, the electric vivifier of all things. Again we find Professor Crookes speaking with approval of Dr. Carnelly’s weighty argument in favor of the compound nature of the so-called elements, based on their analogy to compound radicals.

Until now, alchemy alone, within the historical period and in so-called civilized countries, has succeeded in obtaining a *real element*, or a particle of homogeneous matter—the *Mysterium Magnum* of Paracelsus. But then, that was before Lord Bacon’s time. <note>In the same address, Professor Crookes says: “The first riddle we encounter in chemistry is ‘What are the elements?’ Of the attempts made so far to define or explain an element, none satisfy the demands of the human intellect. The textbooks tell us that an element is ‘a body which has not been decomposed,’ that it is ‘something to which we can add, but from which we can take nothing,’ or ‘a body which increases in weight with every chemical change.’ Such definitions are doubly unsatisfactory: they are provisional and may cease tomorrow to be applicable in any given case. They take their stand not on any attribute of the things to be defined, but on the limitations of human power; they are confessions of intellectual impotence.”</note>

. . . Let us now turn to the upper portion of the scheme. With hydrogen having an atomic weight of 1, there is little room for other elements, except perhaps for hypothetical *Helium*. Dr. Carnelly asks for an element of negative atomic weight; here there is ample room and scope enough for a shadow series of such insubstantialities. Helmholtz says that electricity is probably as atomic as matter; is electricity one of the negative elements, and the luminiferous ether another? Matter, as we now know it, does not exist here; the forms of energy which are apparent in the motions of matter are as yet only latent possibilities. A substance of *negative weight is not inconceivable*. <note>The lecturer quotes Sir George Airy, who says (in *Faraday’s Life and Letters*, Vol. ii, p. 354): “I can easily conceive that there are plenty of bodies around us not subject to this mutual interaction, and therefore not subject to the law of gravitation.”</note> But can we form a clear conception of a body which combines with other bodies in proportions expressible by negative qualities? <note>The *Vedântic* philosophy conceives of such, but then it is not physics, but metaphysics, which Professor Tyndall calls “poetry” and “fiction.”</note>

A genesis of the elements such as is sketched out here would not be confined to our little solar system, but would probably follow the same general sequence of events in every center of energy now visible as a star.

Before the birth of atoms to gravitate toward one another, no pressure could be exercised. However, at the outskirts of the fire-mist sphere—within which everything is protyle—at the shell on which the tremendous forces involved in the birth of a chemical element exert full sway, the fierce heat would be accompanied by gravitation sufficient to keep the newly born elements from flying off into space. As temperature increases, expansion and molecular motion increase; molecules tend to fly apart, and their chemical affinities are weakened. But the enormous pressure of the gravitation of the mass of atomic matter, outside what I may for brevity call the birth-shell, would counteract the action of heat.

Beyond the birth-shell would be a space in which no chemical action could take place, because the temperature there is above what is called the dissociation point for compounds. In this space, the lion and the lamb would lie down together; phosphorus and oxygen would mix without uniting, hydrogen and chlorine would show no tendency toward closer bonds, and even fluorine—that energetic gas which chemists have only isolated within the last month or two—would float about free and uncombined.

# SECTION 12

## SCIENTIFIC AND ESOTERIC EVIDENCE FOR, AND OBJECTIONS TO, THE MODERN NEBULAR THEORY

Recently, Esoteric Cosmogony has frequently been opposed by the phantom of this theory and its resulting hypotheses. "Can this most scientific teaching be denied by your Adepts?" it is asked. "Not entirely," is the reply, "but the admissions of the men of Science themselves *negate it*, and there remains nothing for the Adepts to deny."

To make Science an integral *whole* indeed requires the study of spiritual and psychic nature, as well as physical nature. Otherwise, it will always be like the anatomy of man, discussed in the past by the uninitiated from the perspective of his external side and in ignorance of the internal workings. Even Plato, the greatest philosopher of his country, was guilty, before his Initiation, of such statements as that liquids pass into the stomach through the lungs. Without metaphysics, as Mr. H.J. Slack says, *real* Science is inadmissible.

The nebulae exist, yet the Nebular Theory is wrong. A nebula exists in a state of entire elemental separation. It is gaseous and—something else besides, which can hardly be connected with gases as these are known to Physical Science, and it is self-luminous. But that is all. The sixty-two "coincidences" listed by Professor Stephen Alexander, <note>Smithsonian Contributions, xxi, Art. I, pp 79-97</note> confirming the Nebular Theory, may all be explained by Esoteric Science, though, as this is not an astronomical work, the disproofs are not attempted at present. Laplace and Faye come closer to the correct theory than any others, but of the speculations of Laplace, there remains little in the current theory beyond its general features.

Nevertheless, says John Stuart Mill:

> There is in Laplace's theory nothing speculative; it is an example of legitimate reasoning from a present effect to its past cause; it assumes nothing more than that objects which really exist obey the laws which are known to be obeyed by all terrestrial objects resembling them. <note>System of Logic, p 229</note>

# THE NEBULAR THEORY. EVIDENCE AND OBJECTIONS

From such an eminent logician as Mill, this would be valuable if it could only be proved that "terrestrial objects resembling" celestial objects at such a distance as the nebulae, *resemble those objects in reality, and not only in appearance.*

Another of the fallacies from the Occult standpoint, embodied in the modern theory as it now stands, is the hypothesis that the planets were all detached from the sun—that they are bone of his bone and flesh of his flesh—whereas the sun and the planets are only co-uterine brothers. They have the same nebular origin, but in a different mode from that postulated by modern astronomy.

The many objections raised by some opponents of the modern Nebular Theory against the homogeneity of original diffuse matter, on the ground of the uniformity in the composition of the fixed stars, do not affect the question of that homogeneity at all, but only the theory itself. Our solar nebula may not be completely homogeneous, or rather, it may fail to reveal itself as such to astronomers, and yet be *de facto* homogeneous. Finally, there does not exist one single fact brought forward by the learned objectors against the Nebular Theory (false as it is, and hence, *illogically enough*, fatal to the hypothesis of the homogeneity of matter) that can withstand criticism. One error leads to another. A false premise will naturally lead to a false conclusion, although an inadmissible inference does not necessarily affect the validity of the major proposition of the syllogism. Thus, one may leave every side-issue and inference from the evidence of spectra and lines as simply provisional for the present, and abandon all matters of detail to physical science. First of all, as Science itself teaches, there are two distinct classes of irresolvable nebulae.

The telescope is unable to distinguish between these two classes, but the spectroscope can do so, and it notes an essential difference between their physical constitutions.

The question of the resolvability of the nebulae has often been presented too affirmatively and quite contrary to the ideas expressed by the illustrious experimenter with the spectra of these constellations—Mr. Huggins. It is said that every nebula whose spectrum contains only bright lines is gaseous, and hence is irresolvable; every nebula with a continuous spectrum must eventually be resolved into stars with an instrument of sufficient power. This assumption is contrary both to the results obtained and to spectroscopic theory. The "Lyra" nebula, the "Dumb-bell" nebula, and the central region of the Orion nebula appear resolvable and show a spectrum of bright lines; the nebula of Canes Venatici is not resolvable and gives a continuous spectrum. This is, then, the final word of Physical Science up to the present year, 1888. Mechanical laws will never be able to prove the homogeneity of Primeval Matter, except by inference and as a desperate necessity when no other solution remains—as in the case of Ether. Modern Science is secure only in its own domain and region: within the physical boundaries of our Solar System. Beyond these, every particle of Matter is different from the Matter it knows, and Matter exists in states of which Science can form no idea. *This matter, which is truly homogeneous, is beyond human perception, if perception is restricted merely to the five senses.* We feel its effects through those INTELLIGENCES which are the results of its primeval differentiation. We name them Dhyân Chohans; they are called the “Seven Governors” in the Hermetic works, those to whom Pymander, the “Thought Divine,” refers as the “Building Powers,” and whom Asklepios calls the “Supernal Gods.”

When, therefore, the SECRET DOCTRINE—asserting that conditioned or limited space (location) has no real existence except in this world of illusion, or, in other words, in our perceptive faculties—teaches that every one of the higher worlds, as well as the lower worlds, is interblended with our own objective world; that millions of things and beings are, in terms of location, around and *in* us, just as we are around, with, and in them; this is not just a metaphysical figure of speech, but a sober fact in Nature, however incomprehensible it may be to our senses.

But one must understand the terminology of Occultism before criticizing its assertions. For example, the Doctrine refuses—as Science does, in one sense—to use the words “above” and “below,” or “higher” and “lower,” in reference to invisible spheres, since here those terms have no meaning. Even the terms “East” and “West” are merely conventional, necessary only to aid our human perceptions. For though the Earth has its two fixed points at the North and South poles, both East and West are variable relative to our own position on the Earth’s surface and as a consequence of its rotation from West to East. Hence, when “*other worlds*” are mentioned—whether better or worse, more spiritual or still more material, even though both are invisible—the Occultist does not locate *these* spheres either *outside* or *inside* our Earth, as theologians and poets do; for their location is nowhere in the space *known to* or *conceived by* the uninitiated. They are, as it were, blended with our world—interpenetrating it and being interpenetrated by it. There are millions and millions of worlds and firmaments visible to us; there are even greater numbers beyond those visible to the telescope, and many of the latter kind do not belong to our *objective* sphere of existence. Although they are as invisible as if they were millions of miles beyond our Solar System, they are nevertheless with us, near us, and *within* our own world; they are as objective and material to their respective inhabitants as ours is to us. But, again, the relation of these worlds to ours is not like a series of egg-shaped boxes nested one within the other, like the toys called Chinese nesting boxes; each is entirely under its own special laws and conditions, having no direct relation to our sphere. As already said, the inhabitants of these worlds may, for all we know or feel, be passing *through* and *around* us as if through empty space, their very homes and countries being interblended with ours, yet not disturbing our vision because we do not yet have the faculties necessary for discerning them. But if we can conceive of a world composed of matter even more rarefied (to *our* senses) than the tail of a comet, and thus of inhabitants in it who are as ethereal, in proportion to *their* globe, as we are in comparison with our rocky, hard-crusted Earth, it is no wonder if we do not perceive them, nor sense their presence or even existence. However, in what way is this idea contrary to science? Can we not suppose that men and animals, plants and rocks, are endowed with a completely different set of senses from those we possess? Can their organisms not be born, develop, and exist under other laws of being than those that rule our little world? Is it absolutely necessary that every physical being should be clothed in "coats of skin" like those that Adam and Eve were provided with in the legend of *Genesis*? Bodily existence, however, we are told by more than one man of science, "may exist under very divergent conditions."

# SECTION 14

## GODS, MONADS, AND ATOMS

SOME years ago we remarked that:
> The <term>Esoteric Doctrine</term> may well be called . . . the "thread doctrine," since, like <term>Sûtrâtmâ</term> <note>In the <term>Vedânta</term> Philosophy</note>, it passes through and strings together all the ancient philosophical and religious systems, and reconciles and explains them <note>*Five Years of Theosophy*, "The Septenary Principle," p. 197</note>.

We now say it does more. It not only reconciles the various and apparently conflicting systems, but it checks the discoveries of modern exact science, showing some of them to be necessarily correct, since they are found corroborated in the Ancient Records. All this will, no doubt, be regarded as terribly impertinent and disrespectful—a veritable crime of *lèse-science* <note>A term for a "crime against science."</note>; nevertheless, it is a fact.

Science is, undeniably, ultra-materialistic in our days; but it finds, in one sense, its justification. Nature, behaving ever esoterically *in actu* <note>In action/reality.</note>, and being, as the <term>Kabalists</term> say, *in abscondito* <note>In hiding/secret.</note>, can only be judged by the uninitiated through her appearance, and that appearance is always deceitful on the physical plane. On the other hand, the naturalists refuse to blend physics with <term>metaphysics</term>, or the body with its informing soul and spirit. They prefer to ignore the latter. This is a matter of choice with some, while a minority very sensibly strive to enlarge the domain of physical science by trespassing on the forbidden grounds of <term>metaphysics</term>, which is so distasteful to some materialists. These scientists are wise in their generation. For all their wonderful discoveries will go for nothing and remain forever headless bodies unless they lift the veil of matter and strain their eyes to see *beyond*. Now that they have studied Nature in the length, breadth, and thickness of her physical frame, it is time to remove the skeleton to the second plane and search within the unknown depths for the living and real entity, for its substance—the <term>noumenon</term> of evanescent matter.

It would indeed be a miracle, a completely abnormal occurrence in the realm of probability and logic, if that handful of deniers were the sole guardians of truth, while the millions of believers in Gods, Angels, and Spirits—in Europe and America alone—namely, Greek and Latin Christians, <term>Theosophists</term>, Spiritualists, Mystics, etc., were nothing more than deluded fanatics and hallucinating mediums, often no more than the victims of deceivers and impostors! Systems and mirage-like Worlds. Nevertheless, to the Eastern Occultist—who is essentially an objective Idealist—in the *real* World, which is a Unity of Forces, there is “a connection of all Matter in the Plenum,” as Leibniz would say. This is symbolized by the Pythagorean Triangle.

It consists of ten points inscribed like a pyramid (from one to four) within its three sides, and it symbolizes the Universe in the famous Pythagorean Decad. The single point at the top is a Monad and represents a Unit-Point, which is *the Unity from which everything proceeds*. Everything is of the same essence as it. While the ten points within the equilateral Triangle represent the phenomenal world, the three sides enclosing the pyramid of points are the barriers of *noumenal* Matter, or Substance, that separate it from the world of Thought.

Pythagoras considered a *point* to correspond proportionally to unity, a *line* to 2, a *surface* to 3, and a *solid* to 4. He defined a point as a monad having position and as the beginning of all things; a line was thought to correspond with duality because it was produced by the first motion from an indivisible nature and formed the junction of two points. A surface was compared to the number three because it is the first of all causes found in figures; for a circle, which is the primary of all round figures, comprises a triad consisting of center, space, and circumference. But a triangle, which is the first of all rectilinear figures, is included in a ternary and receives its form according to that number; it was considered by the Pythagoreans to be the author of all sublunary things. The four points at the base of the Pythagorean triangle correspond with a solid or cube, which combines the principles of length, breadth, and thickness, for no solid can have fewer than four extreme boundary points.¹

It is argued that “the human mind cannot conceive of an indivisible unit without annihilating the idea along with its subject.” This is an error, as the Pythagoreans and a number of Seers before them have proved, although special training is needed for this conception, and the profane mind can hardly grasp it. But there are such things as “*Meta-mathematics*” and “*Meta-geometry*.” Even Mathematics, pure and simple, proceeds from the universal to the particular—from the mathematically indivisible point to solid figures. The teaching originated in India and was taught in Europe by Pythagoras, who—throwing a veil over the Circle and the Point, which no living man can define except as incomprehensible abstractions—placed the origin of differentiated cosmic Matter at the base of the Triangle. Thus, the triangle became the earliest of geometrical figures. The author of *New Aspects of Life*, dealing with the Kabalistic Mysteries, objects to the objectification, so to speak, of the Pythagorean conception and the use of the equilateral triangle, calling it a “misnomer.”² His argument that a solid equilateral body—

But this third postulate will hardly be accepted by modern men of Science; like Descartes, they will prefer keeping to the properties of external things which, like extension, are incapable of explaining the phenomenon of motion, rather than accept the latter as an independent Force. They will never become anti-Cartesian in this generation; nor will they admit that:

> This property of inertia is not a purely geometrical property; it points to the existence of something in external bodies which is not extension merely.

This is Leibnitz’s idea as analyzed by Mertz, who adds that he called this “something” Force, and maintained that external things were endowed with Force, and that in order to be the bearers of this Force they must have a Substance, for they are not lifeless and inert masses, but the centers and bearers of Form—a purely Esoteric claim, since *force* was with Leibnitz an *active principle*—the division between Mind and Matter disappearing by this conclusion.

The mathematical and dynamical inquiries of Leibnitz would not have led to the same result in the mind of a purely scientific inquirer. Had he been so, he might have worked out the conception of energy, defined mathematically the ideas of force and mechanical work, and arrived at the conclusion that even for purely scientific purposes it is desirable to look upon force, not as a primary quantity, but as a quantity derived from some other value.

->But, luckily for truth:<-

Leibnitz was a philosopher, and as such he had certain primary principles, which biased him in favor of certain conclusions, and his discovery that external things were substances endowed with force was at once used for the purpose of applying these principles. One of these principles was the law of continuity, the conviction that all the world was connected, that there were no gaps and chasms which could not be bridged over. The contrast of extended thinking substances was unbearable to him. The definition of the extended substances had already become untenable; it was natural that a similar inquiry was made into the definition of mind, the thinking substance.

The divisions made by Leibnitz, however incomplete and faulty from the standpoint of Occultism, show a spirit of metaphysical intuition to which no man of Science, not Descartes, not even Kant, has ever reached. With him there existed ever an infinite gradation of thought. Only a small portion of the contents of our thoughts, he said, rises into the clearness of apperception, “into the light of perfect consciousness.” Many remain in a confused or obscure state, in the state of “perceptions”; but they are there. Descartes denied a soul to the animal; Leibnitz, as do the Occultists, endowed “the whole creation with mental life, this being, according to him, capable of infinite gradations.” And this, as Mertz justly observes:

At once widened the realm of mental life, destroying the contrast of *animate* and *inanimate matter*; it did yet more—it reacted on the conception of matter, of the

extended substance. For it became evident that external or material things presented the property of extension to our senses only, not to our thinking faculties. The bulk through which external things seemed to fill space was a property which they acquired only through the coarseness of our senses. . . Leibnitz followed these arguments to some extent, but he could not rest content in assuming that matter was composed of a finite number of very small parts. His mathematical mind forced him to carry out the argument *to infinity*. And what became of the atoms then? They lost their extension and retained only their property of resistance; they were the centers of force. They were reduced to mathematical points.

But if their extension in space was nothing, their *inner life* was so much fuller. Assuming that inner existence, such as that of the human mind, is a new dimension—not a geometrical but a metaphysical dimension—having reduced the geometrical extension of the atoms to nothing, Leibnitz endowed them with an infinite extension in the direction of their metaphysical dimension. After having lost sight of them in the world of space, the mind has, as it were, to dive into a metaphysical world to find and grasp the real essence of what appears in space merely as a mathematical point. As a cone stands on its point, or a perpendicular straight line cuts a horizontal plane only at one mathematical point, but may extend infinitely in height and depth, so the essences of *real things* have only a point-like existence in this physical world of space, but have an infinite depth of inner life in the metaphysical world of thought. <note>Ibid., p. 144</note>

There are swarms of such *informed* Atoms which, in their turn, inform the molecules, an infinity of Monads, or Elementals proper, and countless spiritual Forces—*Monadless*,² for they are purely incorporeal beings, except under certain laws, when they assume a form—not necessarily *human*. Where does the substance that clothes them—the apparent organism they evolve around their centers—come from? The Formless (Arûpa) Radiations, existing in the harmony of the Universal Will, and being what we call the collective or the aggregate of Cosmic Will on the plane of the subjective Universe, unite an infinity of Monads—each the mirror of its own Universe—and thus individualize for the time being an independent Mind, omniscient and universal; and by the same process of magnetic aggregation they create for themselves objective, visible bodies out of the interstellar Atoms. For Atoms and Monads, associated or dissociated, simple or complex, are, from the moment of the first differentiation, merely the *principles*—corporeal, psychic, and spiritual—of the "Gods"—themselves the Radiations of Primordial Nature. Thus, to the eye of the Seer, the higher Planetary Powers appear under two aspects: the subjective—as *influences*, and the objective—as mystic <term>FORMS</term>, which, under Karmic law, become a Presence. Spirit and Matter are One, as has been repeatedly stated. Spirit is Matter *on the seventh plane*, Matter is Spirit at the lowest point of its cyclic activity; and both are—<term>MÂYÂ</term>.

Atoms are called Vibrations in Occultism, and also, collectively, Sound. This does not conflict with Professor Tyndall's scientific discovery. He traced the entire course of atmospheric vibrations on the lower rung of the ladder of monadic being—and this constitutes the objective part of the process in Nature. He has traced and recorded the speed of their motion and transmission; the force of their impact, their creation of vibrations in the eardrum, and their transmission of these to the otoliths, etc., until the vibration of the auditory nerve begins—and then a new phenomenon occurs: the subjective side of the process, or the sensation of sound. Does he perceive or see it? No, for his specialty is to discover the behavior of matter. But why shouldn’t a psychic or a spiritual seer see it—someone whose inner eye is opened and who can see through the veil of matter? The waves and undulations of science are all produced by atoms propelling their molecules into activity *from within*. Atoms fill the immensity of space, and through their continuous vibration, they are that MOTION which keeps the wheels of life perpetually turning. It is that inner work that produces the natural phenomenon called the correlation of forces. However, at the origin of every such "force," there stands its conscious, guiding noumenon—whether an angel or god, spirit or demon; these are ruling powers, yet they are the same.

As described by seers—those who can see the motion of interstellar shoals and follow them clairvoyantly in their evolution—they are dazzling, like specks of pure snow in radiant sunlight. Their velocity is faster than thought, quicker than any mortal physical eye can follow, and, as far as can be judged from the tremendous speed of their course, the motion is circular. Standing on an open plain, especially on a mountain summit, and gazing into the vast vault above and the spatial infinitudes around, the entire atmosphere seems ablaze with them, the air saturated with these dazzling flashes of light. At times, the intensity of their motion produces flashes like the Northern Lights, the Aurora Borealis. The sight is so marvelous that as the seer gazes into this inner world and feels the scintillating points shoot past him, he is filled with awe at the thought of other, even greater mysteries that lie beyond and within this radiant ocean.

However imperfect and incomplete this explanation of "Gods, Monads, and Atoms" may be, it is hoped that at least some students and Theosophists will feel that there may indeed be a close relationship between materialistic science and occultism, which is the complement and the missing soul of the former.

# SECTION 15

## CYCLIC EVOLUTION AND KARMA

The spiritual evolution of the inner, immortal Man forms the fundamental tenet of the <term>Occult Sciences</term>. To even distantly realize such a process, the student must believe (a) in the ONE Universal Life, independent of Matter (or what Science regards as Matter), and (b) in the individual Intelligences that animate the various manifestations of this Principle. Professor Huxley does not believe in Vital Force; other scientists do. Dr. J. H. Hutchinson Stirling’s work *As regards Protoplasm* has caused significant damage to this dogmatic denial. Professor Beale’s decision also favors a *Vital Principle*; and Dr. B. W. Richardson’s lectures on *Nervous Ether* have been frequently quoted. Thus, opinions are divided.

The ONE LIFE is closely related to the One Law which governs the World of Being—<term>KARMA</term>. Exoterically, this is simply and literally “action,” or rather an “effect-producing cause.” Esoterically, it is quite a different thing in its far-reaching moral effects. It is the unerring LAW OF RETRIBUTION. To tell those who are ignorant of the real significance, characteristics, and profound importance of this eternal, immutable Law that no theological definition of a Personal Deity can give an idea of this impersonal, yet ever-present and active Principle, is to speak in vain. Nor can it be called Providence. For Providence, according to the Theists—Protestant Christians, at any rate—is characterized by a personal male gender, while for Roman Catholics it is a female power. “Divine Providence tempers His blessings to secure their better effects,” Wogan tells us. Indeed “He” modifies them, which <term>Karma</term>—a sexless principle—does not.

Throughout the first two Parts <note>Volume 1 contains Part 1; Volume 2 contains Parts 2 and 3.</note>, it has been shown that, at the first flutter of returning life, <term>Svabhâvat</term>, “*the Mutable Radiance of the Immutable Darkness unconscious in Eternity*,” passes, at every new rebirth of the <term>Kosmos</term>, from—

If a <term>Vedântic</term> <term>Brâhman</term> of the <term>Advaita</term> Sect were asked whether he believed in the existence of God, he would probably answer—just as <term>Jacolliot</term> was answered—“I am myself ‘God’,” while a Buddhist (especially a Sinhalese) would simply laugh and say in reply, “There is no God; no Creation.” Yet the root philosophy of both <term>Advaita</term> and Buddhist scholars is *identical*, and both have the same respect for animal life. This is because both believe that every creature on Earth, however small and humble, “is an immortal portion of the immortal Matter.” For them, "Matter" has an entirely different significance than it does for either a Christian or a Materialist. Both also believe that every creature is subject to <term>Karma</term>.

The answer of the <term>Brâhman</term> would have suggested itself to every ancient philosopher, <term>Kabalist</term>, and <term>Gnostic</term> of the early days. It contains the very spirit of the <term>Delphic</term> and <term>Kabalistic</term> commandments. Esoteric Philosophy solved the problem ages ago of what man *was, is*, and *will be*: his origin, his life-cycle—which is interminable in its duration of successive incarnations or rebirths—and his final absorption into the Source from which he started.

But we can never ask physical science to explain man for us, as the riddle of the Past or of the Future; for no philosopher can tell us even what man is, as known to both physiology and psychology. Doubting whether man was a God or a beast, Science has now connected him with the latter and derives him from an animal. Certainly, the task of analyzing and classifying the human being as a *terrestrial animal* may be left to Science, which <term>Occultists</term>, of all people, regard with veneration and respect. They recognize its foundation and the wonderful work it has done, as well as the progress achieved in physiology and even—to a degree—in biology. 

But man’s *inner, spiritual, psychic*, or even *moral* nature cannot be left to the tender mercies of an ingrained Materialism. Not even the higher psychological philosophy of the West is able, in its present incompleteness and tendency toward a decided Agnosticism, to do justice to the inner man—especially to his higher capacities and perceptions, and to those states of consciousness across the road to which such authorities as <term>Mill</term> draw a strong line, saying, “So far, and no farther shall you go.”

No <term>Occultist</term> would deny that man—together with the elephant and the microbe, the crocodile and the lizard, the blade of grass and the crystal—is, in his physical formation, the simple product of the evolutionary forces of Nature through a numberless series of transformations; but the <term>Occultist</term> explains the case differently.

It is not against zoological and anthropological discoveries based on the fossils of humans and animals that every mystic and believer in a divine soul inwardly revolts, but only against the uncalled-for conclusions built on preconceived theories and made to fit certain prejudices. The premises of scientists may or may not always be true, and as some of these theories live only a short life, the deductions from them must always be one-sided for materialistic evolutionists. Yet it is on the strength of such very fleeting authority that most men of science frequently receive honors where they deserve them the least.<note>We refer those who would regard this statement as an impertinence or irreverence leveled at accepted science to Dr. James Hutchinson Stirling’s work *As Regards Protoplasm*, which is a defense of a vital principle against the molecularists—Huxley, Tyndall, Vogt, and company—and we request them to examine whether it is true or not to say that, though the scientific premises may not always be correct, they are, nevertheless, accepted to fill a gap or a hole in some beloved materialistic hobby. After telling us that all forms of protoplasm consist of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen 'in very complex union,' he continues: 'To this complex combination, the nature of which has never been determined with exactness, the name of *<term>protein</term>* has been applied.' This, plainly, is an identification on Professor Huxley’s own part of protoplasm and protein, and what is said of one being necessarily true of the other, it follows that he admits the nature of protoplasm has never been determined with exactness, and that even in his eyes the *dispute* is still *<term>sub judice</term>*. ...feel so sure that the attributes of matter have not altered under the hand of <term>Protean Evolution</term>? How can any materialist assert with such confidence, as is done by Rossmässler, that:

->This eternal consistency in the essence of phenomena makes it certain that fire and water possessed the same powers at all times and always will possess them.<-

Who are they “who obscure counsel with words without knowledge,” and where were the Huxleys and Büchners when the foundations of the Earth were laid by the Great Law? This same homogeneity of matter and immutability of natural laws, which are so strongly insisted upon by materialism, are a fundamental principle of <term>Occult Philosophy</term>; but this unity rests upon the inseparability of spirit from matter, and, if the two were once divorced, the whole <term>Kosmos</term> would fall back into <term>Chaos</term> and <term>Non-being</term>. Therefore, it is absolutely *false*—and merely another demonstration of the great arrogance of our age—to assert, as men of science do, that all the great geological changes and terrible convulsions of the past have been produced *by ordinary and known physical forces*. For these forces were only the tools and final means for the accomplishment of certain purposes, acting periodically, and apparently mechanically, through an inward impulse mixed with, but beyond, their material nature. There is a purpose in every important act of nature, whose acts are all cyclic and periodical. But because spiritual forces have usually been confused with purely physical ones, the former are denied by science—and therefore, because they are left unexamined, they must remain unknown to it.<note>Men of science will say: We deny this because nothing of the kind has ever come within the scope of our experience. But, as argued by Charles Richet, the psychologist: “So be it, but have you at least demonstrated the contrary? . . . Do not, at any rate, deny *a priori*. Current science is not sufficiently advanced to give you such a right.”—*Mental Suggestion and the Calculus of Probabilities.*</note>

As Hegel says:

> The history of the world begins with its general aim, the realization of the Idea of Spirit—only in an implicit form (in itself), that is, as nature, a hidden, most profoundly hidden, unconscious instinct; and the whole process of history is directed toward making this unconscious impulse a conscious one. Thus appearing in the form of merely natural existence, the natural will—what has been called the subjective side—physical craving, instinct, passion, private interest, as well as opinion and subjective conception, spontaneously present themselves at the very beginning. This vast collection of volitions, interests, and activities constitutes the instruments and means of the <term>World-Spirit</term> for attaining its object, bringing it to consciousness and realizing it. # THE ZODIAC AND ITS ANTIQUITY

The signs of the Zodiac were known and worshipped. These were held in the same adoration as the Sun and Moon, since the
> priests, whom the kings of Judah had appointed to burn incense . . . to Baal, to the sun, to the moon, to the planets, and to all the host of heaven <note>¹ II Kings 23:5</note>

—or to the "twelve signs or constellations," as the marginal note in the English *Bible* explains—had followed these orders for centuries. They were stopped in their idolatry only by King Josiah in 624 B.C.

The *Old Testament* is full of allusions to the twelve zodiacal signs, and the entire framework is built upon them—including heroes, personages, and events. Thus, in the dream of Joseph, who saw eleven "Stars" bowing to the *twelfth*, which was *his* "Star," the Zodiac is referred to. Furthermore, Roman Catholics have discovered in this a prophecy of Christ, who they say is that twelfth Star, while the others represent the *eleven apostles*; the absence of the twelfth star is also regarded as a prophetic allusion to the treachery of Judas. The twelve sons of Jacob are another reference to the same concept, as is correctly pointed out by Villapandus. <note>² *Temple of Jerusalem*, Vol. II Part II, xxx, [from *On Spirits*, Volume 4, p. 58].</note> Sir James Malcolm, in his *History of Persia*, <note>³ Chapter vii, [from *On Spirits*, Volume 4, p. 55].</note> shows that the *Dabistan* echoes all such traditions regarding the Zodiac. He traces its invention to the prosperous days of the Golden Age of Iran, noting that one of these traditions maintains that the spirits (Genii) of the planets are represented in the same shapes and forms they assumed when they appeared to various holy prophets, which led to the establishment of the rites based on the Zodiac.

Pythagoras, and after him Philo Judæus, considered the number 12 to be very sacred.

This duodenary number is *perfect*. It is the number of the signs of the Zodiac, which the sun visits in twelve months. It is to honor that number that Moses divided his nation into twelve tribes, established the twelve cakes <note>⁴ *Leviticus* 24:5.</note> of the showbread, and placed twelve precious stones upon the breastplate of the high priests. <note>⁵ Quoted by De Mirville, *On Spirits*, Volume 4, pp. 58-59.</note>

The reader may be reminded of some opinions expressed regarding the Zodiac by several of the highest authorities in Science.

Newton believed that the invention of the Zodiac could be traced as far back as the expedition of the Argonauts, and Dulaure fixed its origin at 6,500 B.C.—exactly 2,496 years before the creation of the world according to *Biblical* chronology.

Creuzer thought it was very easy to show that most theogonies were intimately connected with religious calendars and were related to the Zodiac as their primary origin. If not to the Zodiac known to us now, then to something very similar to it. He felt certain that the Zodiac and its mystical relations are at the bottom of all mythologies, in one form or another, and that it had existed in its old form for ages before it was presented in its current defined astronomical garb, due to some singular coordination of events. <gloss>1</gloss>

Whether the “genii of the planets”—our Dhyân Chohans of supramundane spheres—showed themselves to “holy prophets” or not, as claimed in the *Dabistân*, it would seem that great laymen and warriors were favored in the same way in the ancient days of Chaldea, when astrological *Magic* and *Theophania* went hand in hand.

Xenophon, no ordinary man, narrates of Cyrus that at the moment of his death, he thanked the Gods and heroes for having so often instructed him themselves about the signs in heaven (*ἐν οὐρανίοις σημείοις*). <gloss>2</gloss>

Unless the science of the Zodiac is admitted to be of the highest antiquity and universality, how can we account for its signs being traced in the oldest theogonies? Laplace is said to have been struck with amazement at the idea of the days of Mercury (Wednesday), Venus (Friday), Jupiter (Thursday), Saturn (Saturday), and others, being related to the days of the week in the same order and with the same names in India as in Northern Europe.

Try, if you can—using the current system of independent civilizations so fashionable in our day—to explain how nations with no common ancestry, no traditions, or birthplace could have succeeded in inventing a kind of celestial phantasmagoria. It is a veritable *imbroglio* of sidereal names, without sequence or objective, having no figurative relation to the constellations they represent, and apparently even less to the phases of our terrestrial life they are meant to signify.
